Therefore it is added: “Behold, I have set before you an open door, which no one is able to shut,” by which we may understand the gate of paradise. Or it may mean that of which the Apostle says: “A great and evident door has been opened to me, and there are many adversaries” (1 Cor. 16:9), signifying that the ears of all had been opened to him for hearing the Gospel. So also here: although heretics resist this bishop, they will nevertheless be unable to close the ears and hearing of the faithful. But because he has little strength—that is, few helpers in this work—the Lord himself, his helper, will subject and humble to him many from the synagogue of Satan, who falsely call themselves Jews, so that they may both be converted to the faith and, conquered, submit. Hence it is added: “Behold, I will cause them to come and [Col. 0622B] worship before your feet,” now, that is, converted to the faith and recognizing the truth of the matter. And behold, at last they shall know that I have loved you—and this deservedly. For you have kept the word of my patience: because I preached patience, you too, reflecting on my words, endured all things patiently.

And I will keep you from the hour of temptation, which is about to come upon the whole world, to test those who dwell on the earth. Behold, I come quickly; hold fast what you have, that no one may take your crown. And whoever conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God, and he shall no longer go out. And I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which descends from heaven from the Lord, and my new name. Whoever has an ear, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

You [Note: [Col. 0622D] Vatican MS: “You,” he says.] have kept [Col. 0622C] the word of my patience, and I also will keep you from the hour of temptation which is coming throughout the whole earth. No one is not tempted, but not all are overcome. Hence the Apostle says: “Let no temptation overtake you except what is human” (1 Cor. 10:13). “Behold, I come quickly” [Note: [Col. 0622D] The persecution of Trajan against Christians is foretold—Trajan having been adopted by Nerva as emperor in A.D. 98—as also those of other emperors hostile to the Christian name.], namely, to deliver you from temptations and crown you for your patience. Therefore hold fast what you have; let no one be able to separate you from the steadfastness of your faith, so that no one may take your crown; let no one steal from you the place appointed beforehand for you.

And whoever conquers, I will make him a pillar in the temple of my God. For such pillars were Peter, James, and John, of whom the Apostle says: “Those who seemed to be pillars of the Church” (Gal. 2:9). Upon [Col. 0622D] these the Church has been established and founded, according to the saying: “I have strengthened its pillars” (Ps. 74:4); [Col. 0623A] 307 and the Apostle: “Built upon the foundation of the apostles and prophets” (Eph. 2:10). For by their teaching and examples the Church is governed and sustained until the end. “And he shall no longer go out”: whoever, then, is separated from the Church should know that he is not yet a conqueror.

“And I will write upon him the name of my God, and the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, which descends from heaven from God, and my new name.” Not only, he says, will I write my name upon him, so that they may be called Christians from Christ; but also the name of my God, so that they themselves may be called gods, according to the saying: “I said, You are gods” (Ps. 81:6). Moreover, I shall write the name of the city of my God, the new Jerusalem, so that, just as that city is universally called the bride of Christ, so the soul of each person may be called so individually [Col. 0623B]. Hence the Apostle says: “For I have betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a chaste virgin to Christ” (2 Cor. 11:2). But that Jerusalem is called the bride of Christ, hear this same man say at the end of this book: “I saw,” he says, “the new city Jerusalem descending from heaven from God, prepared like a bride adorned for her husband.”

We may also understand as Christ’s new name that name which was explained to him by the angel; for thus it is written: “And you shall call his name Jesus” (Luke 1:31), which is interpreted “Savior”; for no one is saved unless marked by this name.

And write to the angel of the church of Laodicea: These things says the Amen, the faithful and true witness, who is the beginning of the creation of God. I know your works: you are neither cold nor [Col. 0623C] hot. Would that you were cold or hot! But because you are lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I shall begin to vomit you out of my mouth.

For Christ is called *Amen*, which naturally signifies “true” in Hebrew. Thus let it be said: These things says he who says of himself: “I am the way, the truth, and the life” (John 14:6); for *truth* and *true* signify the same thing. He is the faithful and true witness, as has already been explained above. He is the beginning of God’s creation, from whom, namely, every creature took its origin. “I know your works: you are neither cold nor hot.” For this bishop behaved so shrewdly according to the times that he favored both the good and the evil alike; hence it could not easily be discerned to which party he chiefly belonged [Note: [Col. 0623D] The bishop of Laodicea, whose name is unknown, is rebuked because good and evil persons were equally acceptable to him; thus his faith was rendered doubtful. Since he labored under slothfulness in God’s service, he incurred divine indignation. Lukewarmness is also abominable to God and unworthy of supreme lordship and [Col. 0624D] goodness.].

Therefore it follows: “Would that you were cold or hot,” so that you might not be able through your hypocrisy to deceive God’s people [Col. 0623D]. “But because you are lukewarm and neither cold nor hot, I shall begin to vomit you out of my mouth.” It is as though he said: There is a serpent in my [Note: [Col. 0624D] Vatican MS: “a grievous [thing] even to me.”] stomach; you make me nauseated; I can no longer endure you. Therefore I shall cast you from my mouth and shall remember your name no more.

Because you say: I am rich, and have become wealthy, and need nothing; and you do not know that you are wretched and miserable and poor and blind and naked. I advise you to buy from me [Col. 0624A] gold refined by fire, that you may become rich, and put on white garments, so that the shame of your nakedness may not appear; and anoint your eyes with eye-salve, that you may see. Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline; be zealous, therefore, and repent.

You, I say, claim and reckon with yourself that you lack nothing; and thus, passing by with closed eyes, whether good or evil things happen, you do not think that they concern you. And you do not know that you are wretched and miserable, deprived of every happiness; poor in spiritual riches; blind, having lost discernment and the light of the heart; and naked of the garments of good works [Note: [Col. 0624D] Some seem to themselves to possess enough virtue because they have been placed in some lofty rank; but then they should labor all the more lest they become inferior to their office.].

But trust my counsels, and it will go well with you. I advise you to buy from me gold refined by fire, that you may become rich. For this fiery and refined gold, by which people are made rich, is charity and the discernment of [Col. 0624B] good and evil. For it always burns and is so inflamed in love of God and neighbor that it cannot be extinguished, according to the saying: “Many waters could not extinguish charity” (Song 8:7). Without it no one will be rich; for whoever offends against it, even if he observes the whole law, has nevertheless become guilty of all.

It follows: “And put on white garments, so that the shame of your nakedness may not appear.” For whoever is not clothed in these garments, and does not cleanse the flesh with which he is clothed from the stains and filth of vices, will appear ashamed at the judgment, an object of mockery before the eyes of all. He is further commanded to anoint his eyes with eye-salve, which is indeed a medicine necessary for the eyes; and because he had been blinded by avarice and greed, let him anoint the eyes of his mind with generosity, mercy, and the anointing of charity [Col. 0624C], so that, once the darkness of every vice has been wiped away, he may receive the light of brightness.

But because the bishop might have been angered by so great a rebuke, he appropriately adds words of goodwill: “Those whom I love I rebuke and discipline,” according to the saying, 308 “He disciplines every son whom he receives” (Heb. 12:6). Therefore emulate virtues, emulate the better gifts, and repent, and you shall be saved.

I stand at the door and knock. If anyone hears my voice and opens the door, I shall enter in to him and dine with him, and he with me on my throne, just as I too conquered and sat with my Father on his throne. Whoever has ears, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.

For Christ stands at the door, and his voice knocks daily; daily the evangelical preaching resounds in our ears [Col. 0624D]. Hence the Apostle says: “Reprove,” he says, “exhort in season and out of season” (2 Tim. 4:2). For the ears are gates through which Christ enters the dwelling-place of the breast. If anyone opens them and hears the voice of him who knocks, Christ will immediately enter into the lodging of that person’s mind and dwell there. Therefore it has so often been said above: “Whoever has ears, let him hear what the Spirit says to the churches.”

But what does this mean: “And I shall dine with him, and he with me,” except that we shall use the same food, be refreshed by the same [Col. 0625A] bread, and be filled by the same teaching? And my food indeed is “to do the will of my Father who is in heaven” (John 4). Whoever feeds on this food with me will dine with me, and I with him [Note: [Col. 0625D] Since God is so generous toward us and such splendid rewards are promised by him, who would not contend for him with his whole heart and endure all things for his greater glory?].

He promises the conquerors [Note: [Col. 0625D] Vatican MS: “to sit with him on the throne.”] that they shall sit with him in his kingdom, so that they may understand that they receive authority to judge over nations and kingdoms. Hence he himself [Col. 0626A] says: “You who have followed me shall sit upon twelve thrones, judging the twelve tribes of Israel” (Matt. 19:28). He too conquered and captured all his enemies, and sits together with his Father upon his throne, according to the saying: “The Father judges no one, but has given all judgment to the Son” (John 5:22).

## BOOK TWO

[Col. 0625]

## CHAPTER IV

[Col. 0625A]

After these things I saw, and behold, a door opened in heaven, and the first voice which I heard, like a trumpet speaking with me, saying: Come up here, and I shall show you what must happen after these things. Immediately I was in the Spirit, and behold, [Col. 0625B] a throne was set in heaven, and one seated upon the throne; and he who sat was like the appearance of a jasper and sardius stone [Note: [Col. 0625D] Called upward by contemplation of mind, John ascends to heaven and beholds the Lord seated upon the throne. Cassiodorus associates the colors of gems with him in figurative speech and expounds the description of the vision excellently.].

“After these things,” he says, “I looked and saw the whole structure of the Church, and whatever was to occur until the consummation of the age. And behold, a door was opened in heaven.” In this place heaven means the holy Church, as we frequently find in the Gospel; for example: “The kingdom of heaven is like a net cast into the sea” (Matt. 13:47), and similar passages, when it speaks of the Church. Its door is never shut; its gate stands open to all; it repels no one who comes to it. Whoever is excluded or does not enter is at fault not because of the door, but because of the person entering.

The first voice, which spoke with him, lofty and exalted like a trumpet [Col. 0625C], was an angelic voice announcing these things. It is rightly compared to a trumpet because human frailty can scarcely bear the inspiration of the Holy Spirit, of whose voice it is said elsewhere: “Suddenly there came from heaven a sound like that of a rushing mighty Spirit” (Acts 2:2). Let us hear what this voice said: “Come up here, and I shall show you there what must happen after these things.” This ascent was not of the body but of the mind. “Come up here,” he says; raise your mind, widen your sight, and contemplate in a single glance of the mind those things which cannot be seen with bodily eyes.

When he had heard these things, “immediately I was in the Spirit”: I felt that I had nothing carnal, nothing of bodily weight; but, caught up in the Spirit and in ecstasy of mind, I immediately received another vision [Note: [Col. 0625D] Having given, in the preceding sections, the account of the first vision, blessed John proceeds in this and the following chapters to speak of the second revelation, in which Christ did not present himself in human form, but God the Father appeared to him in all splendor and majesty of throne. Accordingly, the divine throne, furnished with most precious gems; thunderings and lightnings proceeding from it; the choir of twenty-four [Col. 0626D] elders around it offering him golden crowns; and four living creatures placed beneath it are described.]. “And behold, a throne was set [Col. 0626A] in heaven.”

This throne, which blessed John saw set in heaven, is the teachers of the Church, in whom the Lord sits and dwells. For the soul of the righteous person is the throne of wisdom. He saw the Lord seated upon this throne, whose appearance was like the sight of jasper and sardius stone. Jasper has a green [Col. 0626B] color, while sardius is bright and fiery. Therefore our Lord wished to appear in such colors, to show us what we ought to seek. He has the color of jasper because he is always green, always living, always immortal, and never comes to dryness. He also has the color of sardius, since our God is a burning fire. In this appearance he once deigned to appear also to Moses. Let us too burn, inflamed with the fervor of charity, and say with the Apostle: “Who shall separate us from the charity of Christ? Tribulation, or distress, or famine, or nakedness?” (Rom. 8:35), and the rest.

And there was a rainbow around the throne, like the appearance of an emerald. For the emerald is green like grass, and by it we understand immortality, which is always green and never comes to dryness. The rainbow, that is, the heavenly bow, has two principal colors: one fiery, the other blue and greenish like water. The red indeed signifies martyrdom, while the green signifies baptism [Note: [Col. 0626D] Here is St. Bruno’s interpretation. Since he supports it with no arguments, it may seem to some obscure, or even drawn merely from the mentality of that age. But whoever considers the nature of baptism and the designation of the newly baptized will immediately see that this is an excellent interpretation, wholly consistent with Scripture and sound reason. Baptism is administered through water; the newly baptized are called *neophytes*, a word which in its Greek origin means “newly planted,” that is, planted in the Church of Christ, in its grace and righteousness. In Scripture, moreover, “the righteous shall flourish like a palm,” which is certainly green; and a certain righteous man, being blessed by God, shall be like a tree transplanted by waters, . . . “and its leaf shall be green,” etc. Jer., ch. 17.]. No one, therefore, shall approach God’s throne or receive greenness and immortality unless he passes either through martyrdom or is washed in baptism. Let those who wish to be around the sun, then, be a rainbow.

And around the throne were twenty-four seats, and upon the thrones twenty-four elders sitting, clothed in white garments, and with golden crowns on their heads. What else [Note: [Col. 0626D] Vatican MS: “And what else.”], he says, did I see after the rainbow, except twenty-four seats around the throne and as many elders [Col. 0627A] sitting upon them? I understand these twenty-four seated around the throne of God to be the twelve patriarchs and an equal number of apostles. Jacob begot the twelve patriarchs according to the flesh, and from them sprang the other saints of the Old Testament. Christ chose the twelve apostles, from whom the entire multitude of the Church grew. Hence it is written: “In place of your fathers, sons have been born to you” (Ps. 44:17).

The twenty-four seats are the twelve tribes, in which the aforesaid patriarchs hold primacy, and the twelve churches over which the apostles presided. For even to this day every bishop is accustomed to call the church entrusted to him his seat. All these were clothed in white garments, clean from sin, since they had been invited to Christ’s banquet [Col. 0627B]. They had golden crowns on their heads, by which we understand that they had conquered all their enemies: “For no one shall be crowned unless he has contended lawfully” (2 Tim. 2:5). Hence the Apostle, because he had fought well, says of himself: “Henceforth there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness” (ibid., v. 8).

And lightnings, voices, and thunderings proceeded from the throne. We said above that the teachers of the Church are the throne of God. From this throne, then, proceed lightnings, voices, and thunderings. For the judgments hurled from their mouths, like lightnings and fiery arrows, scatter the whole multitude of vices and heretics. These do not occur without voices and thunderings, while holy preaching resounds loudly in the Church and [Col. 0627C] strikes a certain terror of the future judgment into its hearers. Imagine, then, some teacher preaching in the Church, and you will immediately hear what lightnings of judgments, what voices of both Testaments, what thunderings of threatening words proceed from his mouth.

And seven burning lamps before the throne, which are the seven spirits of God. For he saw lamps by which the throne was illuminated; and, explaining what they were, he says, “which are the seven spirits of God,” that is, the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit. Therefore let teachers preach confidently, illuminated by so great a light. For, as the Lord says, it is not they who speak, but the Holy Spirit who speaks in them.

And before the throne there was as it were a sea of glass, like crystal. Before the throne, he says, there was as it were [Col. 0627D] a sea of glass—that is, the clear water of baptism. It is before the throne because holy teachers never in any way forget this water. It is said to be like crystal because crystal is made from water; yet, when hardened, it has more the nature of fire than of water. Thus the saints, regenerated from water, are changed into crystal, because, filled with the fire of the Holy Spirit, they appear outwardly as they are inwardly.

And in the midst of the throne and around the throne were four living creatures, full of eyes before and behind. And the first living creature was like a lion; the second living creature like a calf; the third living creature had a face like a man; and [Col. 0628A] the fourth living creature was like a flying eagle. These four living creatures are the four evangelists. They are rightly seen in the midst of the throne and around it, because their teaching fills all things, prelates and subjects alike. They are full of eyes before and behind because they behold the past, 310 present, and future. They do not fear the missiles of enemies; they do not fear the pronouncements of heretics, because they foresee everything and nothing can happen to them unexpectedly.

“The first living creature was like a lion,” by which we understand the evangelist Mark, who, like a lion roaring through the wilderness, begins his Gospel by saying: “A voice crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the Lord, make his paths straight” (Luke 3:4). The second living creature, like a calf, is Luke, who begins from sacrifice—which was most commonly offered from [Col. 0628B] calves—saying: “In the days of Herod of Judaea there was a priest” (Luke 1:5), etc. The third living creature, whose face was like that of a man, is understood to be Matthew, who, describing Christ’s birth and incarnation, declares that he was fully man and born from human beings, saying: “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, son of David, son of Abraham” (Matt. 1). But we do not doubt that the fourth living creature, like a flying eagle, was blessed John, whose words these are; like an eagle flying higher than the rest, he shows Christ, the Son of God, to be God without beginning, saying: “In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was with God, and the Word was God” (John 1:1). Therefore, whoever wishes to know these living creatures should inspect and read their “face,” that is, the beginnings of their sayings, and will immediately be able to understand what and of what sort they are.

And each of the four living creatures had six wings, and they were full of eyes around and within, and they had no rest day and night, saying: Holy, holy, holy, Lord God almighty, who was, and who is, and who is to come.—Each, he says, of the aforesaid four living creatures had six wings, which together make twenty-four. Therefore there are as many wings as the aforesaid elders; hence we rightly understand them to be the wings of the living creatures, for upon these wings the Gospels have flown throughout all lands. But because the Old and New Testament are the same [Note: [Col. 0627D] Vatican MS: “say the same [things].”] and signify the same things, not only the apostles but also the patriarchs are deservedly called the wings of the living creatures.

[Col. 0628D] These living creatures are full of eyes both around and within, so that they may foresee visible and invisible enemies, external and internal. Their unceasing cry day and night—“Holy, holy, holy, Lord God almighty”—signifies the mystery of the Trinity. For although “holy” is said three times, “Lord God almighty” is said only once, so that he who is divided in persons may nevertheless be believed one in majesty, power, and substance. As for what follows, “who is, and who was, and who is to come,” we have already explained it above.

And when the four living creatures gave glory and [Col. 0629A] honor and blessing to him who sits upon the throne, who lives for ages of ages, the twenty-four elders fell down before him who sits upon the throne, and worshipped him who lives for ages of ages, and cast their crowns before the throne, saying: Worthy are you, O Lord our God, to receive glory and honor and power, because you created all things, and because of your will they existed and were created.

When, he says, the living creatures praised, blessed, and glorified God, the twenty-four elders immediately fell down at their voices and worshipped the living and true God. For what saint, hearing the Gospel, would not give thanks to the Father, “who did not spare his own Son, but delivered him up for us all” (Rom. 8:32), by whose teaching and passion we have been redeemed? [Col. 0629B] They cast their crowns before the throne because they attribute victory, triumph, and crown not to their own strength but to God the conqueror. Had King Nebuchadnezzar done this, perhaps he would not have lost his kingdom so quickly. But because these recognize that they have received all things from God, they say not of themselves but of the Lord: “Worthy are you, O Lord our God, to receive glory and honor and power.” Why so? Because it was not we, but you, who created all things; and they existed by your will, that is, in the ordering of your wisdom, even before they were made; and now indeed they have been created and distributed, each in its own time: “For all things are set forth in your will” (Eph. 1:9).

## CHAPTER V

[Col. 0629C] And I saw in the right hand of him who sat upon the throne a book written within and without, sealed with seven seals [Note: [Col. 0629D] Meanwhile John saw a book in the right hand of the Father seated upon the throne, written within and without, because in the Law some things are still hidden while some are known to be manifest. It appeared sealed with seven seals [Col. 0630D], that is, with the sevenfold Spirit, because the mysteries of the Lord are always unknown until the appointed time. CASSIODORUS.].

This book, which blessed John says he saw in the right hand of him who sat upon the throne, is understood as the knowledge of both Testaments. The Lord is said to hold it in his right hand because nothing is hidden from his knowledge. It is written within and without because it is interpreted one way according to the letter and another according to spiritual understanding. But what do we understand by the seven seals except Christ’s birth, passion, resurrection, ascension, baptism, judgment, and recompense of merits? Sealed by these, it could not be understood even by the learned and wise men of the Law. For though the prophet says, “Behold, a virgin shall conceive and bear a son” (Isa. 7:18 [Col. 0629D]), nevertheless, because the book is sealed, the Jews do not understand this. Of the passion and resurrection it is written: “I lay down and slept; and I rose, because the Lord sustained me” (Ps. 3:6). But which of the Jews understands this? So also of the ascension: “God ascended amid jubilation, and the Lord amid the sound of a trumpet” (Ps. 46:6). Of baptism: “Wash yourselves; be clean” (Isa. 1:16). Of judgment: “O God, give your judgment to the king, and your righteousness to the king’s son” (Ps. 71:1). The Scriptures are full of the recompense of merits; [Col. 0630A] yet these things are not understood, because the book is sealed.

And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming in a loud voice: Who is worthy to open the book and break its seals? And no one in heaven, nor on earth, nor under the earth, was able to open the book or look upon it. And I wept greatly because no one was found worthy to open the book or to see it.

This mighty and wise angel is any preacher of the Church, who, considering the divine mysteries and the depth of the Scriptures, marvels and says: Who is worthy to open the book [Note: [Col. 0630D] Vatican MS: “this book.”]? Who can unlock mysteries so hidden? Who will break its seals and resolve its questions, so difficult? Who is wise and understands these things? “And no one in heaven or on earth was able to open [Col. 0630B] the book.” For no one could open or understand this book by the acuteness of his own intellect unless he who composed and sealed it had opened it. Neither those who are in heaven, that is, ecclesiastical men; nor those on earth, that is, philosophers and wise men; nor those under the earth, that is, evil spirits, were able to understand or see this book, until Christ opened it and gave his disciples understanding that they might understand the Scriptures. Blessed John wept greatly because no one was found worthy to open the book. For he knew that the world could not otherwise be converted to the faith, nor the Church built, unless that book were opened and its testimonies made manifest.

[Col. 0630C] And one of the elders said to me: Do not weep; behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has conquered, to open the book and break its seven seals.

This one of the elders who comforted him, lest he should weep, can be understood as no one better than John himself, for he too was one of the elders. Remembering, therefore, that at Christ’s passion the veil of the temple was rent and the tombs opened, he restrained himself from weeping, reflecting and saying to himself: “Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah has conquered.” For in the blessing of Judah it is written among other things: “You have gone up to the prey, my son; you have lain down like a lion, and like a lioness: who shall rouse him?” (Gen. 49:9). This was fulfilled in Christ’s passion, when he ascended the cross for prey, upon which he conquered all his enemies [Col. 0630D]; and when he lay down like a lion, since, being stronger, he rose from sleep.

He himself is the root of David, of whom the Prophet says: “A rod shall come forth from the root of Jesse, and a flower shall rise from his root” (Ps. 11:1). And the Psalmist says: “The Lord has sworn truth and will not fail in it: of the fruit of your womb I shall set one upon your throne” (Ps. 131:11). He therefore conquered in order to open the book and break its seven seals.

And I saw, and behold, in the midst of the throne and of the four living creatures, and in the midst of the elders, a lamb standing as though [Col. 0631A] slain, having seven horns and seven eyes, which are the seven spirits of God, sent into all the earth.

This is the lamb of whom it is written: “Behold the Lamb of God, who takes away the sins of the world” (John 1:29). He is rightly said to stand in the midst of the throne, the four living creatures, and the elders because he always dwells with his saints and never forsakes them [Note: [Col. 0631D] This lamb is also said to stand in the midst between the throne and the four living creatures, because Christ is mediator between God, angels, and human beings. So Cornelius a Lapide. It is a very ancient custom in the Church to represent Christ under the figure of a lamb in mosaics, paintings, etc.; and in the Mass, too, after the ordinance of Pope Sergius, he is invoked under this name. For John the Baptist called our Redeemer the Lamb of God. He appeared as though slain because he had risen victorious from the dead and was no longer to die.], as he himself says: “I shall not leave you or forsake you” (John 14:18); and again: “I am with you all days, even to the consummation of the age” (Matt. 28:20).

He saw him as though slain because there is nothing which the saints of God hold more in memory than the death of their Savior. The seven horns [Note: [Col. 0631D] Vatican MS omits “seven.”] and eyes are the gifts of the Holy Spirit, by which we are defended and [Col. 0631B] enlightened.

And he came and took the book from the right hand of him who sat upon the throne; and when he had opened the book, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell before the Lamb, each having harps and golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.

According to his humanity, Christ our Lord received the book from the right hand of him who sat upon the throne, from whom, according to his divinity, all wisdom and knowledge proceed. When he had opened it, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell before the Lamb, because, after all the holy apostles and teachers had understood the Scriptures, they gave thanks to Christ our Lord, who through the Holy Spirit both gave them understanding and caused them there to know his benefits [Col. 0631C] [Note: [Col. 0631D] Vatican MS: “caused them to know them there.”].

Holy teachers possess harps, by the sweet melody of which they calm human hearts swollen with sins. Such a harpist was the Apostle, at whose preaching even the philosophers were astonished. They also possess golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints. For the prayers of the saints are full of incense because nothing breathes a sweeter fragrance to the Lord.

And they sang a new song, saying: “You are worthy, O Lord our God, to receive the book and to open its seals, because you were slain, and redeemed us to God by your blood, from every tribe and tongue and people and nation; and you made us a kingdom and priests to our God, and they shall reign upon the earth.” The saints sing [Col. 0631D] a new song—the song, that is, of Christ’s passion and of our redemption. It was indeed new, and unheard by all before that time. They sang, therefore, and said: You indeed received the book from the right hand of him who sits upon the throne, and you are truly worthy, O Lord our God, to receive the book. For who is more worthy to undertake the exposition of the law than the teacher and author of the law himself—he who not only taught and acted, but acted what he taught? For thus it is written: “I made the former account, O Theophilus, concerning all that Jesus began to do and to teach” (Acts 1:1). Therefore he taught the law; he opened and disclosed its seals and hidden mysteries. He died, as the law commanded: “For thus it was necessary for Christ to suffer and rise from the dead, in order that he might redeem us from death” (Luke 24:46). Hence it is added: [Col. 0632B] “Because he was slain, and you redeemed us to God by your blood.” But whence did you redeem us? From every tribe and tongue and people and nation. For he is not God of the Jews only, but also of the Gentiles. From all nations, therefore, he called to the faith those whom he redeemed by his blood. It follows: “And you made us”—that is, the Christian people—“a kingdom to our God,” because he himself reigns in us, “and priests,” to whom we daily offer acceptable sacrifices. At this point, however, the person changes, and the voice of Scripture is introduced: “and they shall reign upon the earth.”

> [Note: Col. 0631D. Vatican manuscript: “The saints, he says, sang.”]
>
> [Note: Col. 0631D–0632D. The thanks which the saints render to Christ for the common salvation he has wrought must always be rendered by us, but especially in the sacrifice of the Mass, in which the mysteries of our restoration are renewed.]
>
> [Note: Col. 0632D. Although Christ the Lord, through the hypostatic union, received what properly belongs to divinity, nevertheless by his passion and death he specially merited certain things: namely, the glory of his body, the establishment of the Church, its spread throughout the whole world, the authority also to judge all nations, and finally the knowledge of revealing the secrets of heaven. Thus Cornelius a Lapide and other expositors.]
>
> [Note: Col. 0632D. Vatican manuscript: “For who will more worthily undertake the exposition of the law?”]
>
> [Note: Col. 0632D. Vatican manuscript: “acceptable sacrifices are offered.”]

And I saw and heard the voice of many angels around the throne, and of the living creatures and elders; and their number was thousands of thousands, saying with a loud voice: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power, [Col. 0632C] and divinity, and wisdom, and strength, and honour, and glory, and blessing.” For first the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders, by whom we understand the whole primitive Church, praising Christ, declared him worthy both to open the book and to loose its seals. But now the voice of many angels—that is, of all teachers who have existed from their time or shall exist—is added. Since they are innumerable, by naming an infinite number he says that they are thousands of thousands. In answer to the voice of the elders, and repeating the same thing, they say: “Worthy is the Lamb who was slain to receive power and divinity.” This is as though he said: He whom the Jews consider dead and inglorious is worthy to be honoured, [Col. 0632D] glorified, and blessed; worthy [Col. 0633A] to be proclaimed strong, wise God, and most just.

> [Note: Col. 0632D. Vatican manuscript: “He whom the Jews consider dead and inglorious.”]

And every creature which is in heaven, and which is upon earth, and which is beneath the earth, and which is in the sea, and all things that are in it, I heard all saying: “To him who sits upon the throne and to the Lamb, blessing and honour and glory and power for ever and ever.” And the four living creatures said, “Amen”; and the twenty-four elders fell upon their faces and worshipped. First the four living creatures and the elders, then all the teachers, and afterward every creature praise and bless God. The creature in heaven is the orders of angels; that upon earth, righteous people, now raised above earthly things; that beneath the earth, sinners or evil spirits, [Col. 0633B] whom the Church will judge. Those in the sea mean all who live in this world. “For every spirit praises the Lord” (Psalm 156:6). And the four living creatures said, “Amen,” affirming, that is, the praises already spoken. Therefore the twenty-four, rejoicing, fell upon their faces and worshipped God, who gave such glory and power to his Son.

> [Note: Col. 0633D. Vatican manuscript: “whom the Church points out.”]

313

## CHAPTER VI

And I saw that the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals, and I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder: “Come and see.” And I saw, and behold, a white horse; and he who sat upon it had a bow, and a crown was given to him, and he went forth conquering [Col. 0633C] in order to conquer.

For there are seven seals, seven churches, and seven days in which all preaching takes place. The seven seals are so connected with one another that whoever knows one has no uncertainty about the others. To whom, therefore, one seal is opened, none is shut; and conversely, to whom one is shut, none is opened. For one who does not believe Christ’s nativity understands nothing of the passion, resurrection, ascension, baptism, judgment, or recompense of merits; and so likewise in the other matters. Thus the seven seals are seven mysteries in which our faith is chiefly contained. All preaching, therefore, and all instruction in our faith is incomplete if these seven seals are not unsealed. Consequently, to open one of the seals means nothing else than to begin with any one of these matters and then to unseal the rest.

Let us see, therefore, what he says. “And I saw,” he says, “that the Lamb had opened one of the seven seals.” In the first Church the Lamb opened one of the seven seals when the first preaching began; and this was the greatest and principal controversy: that concerning the incarnation of the Son of God. Thus churches succeed one another from the first to the last, so that they never exceed the number seven. “And I heard one of the four living creatures saying, as with a voice of thunder: ‘Come and see.’” For these four living creatures wrote one and the same preaching, although in some respects they seem to relate different things. Thus they write Christ’s words and cry out in a lofty voice, since they speak to the whole world. But what do they say? “Come and see.” Draw near to the Gospel: the book has been opened; see and understand what it contains. “And behold, a white horse.” This white horse—entirely beautiful and without blemish—means any doctor of the Church. “And he who sat upon it had a bow.” This is [Col. 0634B] Christ our Lord, of whom it is written: “You will ride upon your horses, and your chariots are salvation” (Habakkuk 3:8). But what is meant by the bow except his preaching? From it proceed, like arrows, the sayings of truth, wounding all enemies. “And a crown was given to him, and he went forth conquering in order to conquer.” For daily Christ goes out to battle through his servants; daily he fights and overthrows the armies of his enemies, and is crowned as often as he works victory in his saints.

> [Note: Col. 0633D. Vatican manuscript: “To whom, therefore, one of the seals is opened.”]
>
> [Note: Col. 0633D. All interpreters agree that this chapter consists of figures, riddles, and mysteries, which each person endeavours, according to his own study and meditation, to draw toward his own view. Some follow a moral interpretation, others a historical one, and others a mystical or spiritual interpretation, as does our Bruno. Yet it is beyond doubt that different states of the Church are described by these things.]

And when he had opened the second seal, I heard the second living creature saying: “Come and see.” And another horse, red, went forth; and to him who sat upon it was given power to take peace from the earth, so that people [Col. 0634C] should kill one another; and a great sword was given to him.

The Lamb, he says, opened the second seal because once again the Lord sent his servants to preach the Gospel: this is what he means. “And I heard the second living creature saying: ‘Come and see.’” The second living creature which invites us to come and see is the second preaching. For although the preachings of teachers are innumerable, they are nevertheless said to be only seven, because there are seven days in which they occur. When the first preachers had died, others succeeded them, and they too preached the Gospel. But because in their time preaching increased greatly in the Church, another red horse is said to have gone forth. The red horse, bloody with the blood of the saints, means the tyrants who persecuted Christ’s martyrs—such as Nero, who killed the apostles themselves. The devil sits upon this horse, because with the bridle of his wickedness he drives it headlong into every crime. This one takes and removes peace from the earth, because, as prince of discord and enemy of peace, he continually harasses humankind by his snares and temptations. [Col. 0635A] He causes people to kill one another and to wage civil wars both against him and against one another. A great sword was given to him, because he deceives by cutting down people in many ways: one he kills and destroys through pride, another through greed, another through lust, and another in some other way.

> [Note: Col. 0634D. For easier understanding of what follows, note that the three following horses—namely, the red, black, and pale—are first opposed to the white and favourable horse, whose rider is Christ. For it is clear that the other three are not Christ: the second, the red horse, disturbs the peace of the earth; the third, the black, has a deceitful balance; the fourth has Death as its rider and Hell as its companion, who carry out that slaughter. This is Cornelius’s interpretation, though he acknowledges that others interpret them differently.]

And when he had opened the third seal, I heard the third living creature saying: “Come and see.” And behold, a black horse; and he who sat upon it had a balance in his hand. And I heard, as it were, a voice in the midst of the [four] living creatures saying: “Two pounds of wheat for one denarius, and three two-pound measures of barley for one denarius; and do not harm the wine and oil.”

The third seal is opened because the third preaching succeeds, and again blessed John is invited to see. “And behold, a black horse”: namely, the persecutors of the Church, [Col. 0635B] who, because they live wickedly and subject themselves to every luxury and pleasure, are not undeservedly called black. “And he who sat upon it had a balance in his hand.” This is that evil spirit who, though he is most wicked of all, nevertheless pretends to possess the instruments of justice. Yet no one can trade with this most wicked merchant without eventually discovering that he has been deceived. Therefore a voice issuing from the midst of the four living creatures sets a price on things, prescribing how and for how much they ought to be bought or sold. Scripture and the teachers always instruct us how we must beware of the devil’s deceits.

“Two pounds of wheat for one denarius, and three two-pound measures of barley for one denarius.” Thus, he says, let it be sold and bought; his balance is false, and no one should wish to trust it. Let two pounds of wheat have the price of one denarius. If this is understood literally, this wheat will seem excessively expensive. Therefore it is of another kind and a more excellent nature, nourishing not the body but the soul. By it we understand the teaching of faith and Holy Scripture. The two pounds are the two Testaments, of the same weight, the same measure, and the same price; neither has force without the other. Therefore they are bought not for two denarii but for one. This denarius signifies eternal life, which the Lord promised he would give to those who labour well in God’s vineyard. For it is written: “Having made an agreement with the workers for a daily denarius, he sent them into his vineyard” (Matthew 20:12). [Col. 0635D] Whoever, therefore, desires to attain this denarius should carry these two pounds of wheat with him, feed upon them, and never forget them.

By the three two-pound measures of barley, which are bought for the same denarius, is understood the faith of the Trinity. Since no one has ever been able in this life to attain to its kernel and most profound understanding, it is rightly compared not with wheat but with barley. Hence very few do not fear not only to dispute about it but even to think about it; yet they shall receive the denarius for it, provided that they believe, even though they do not understand. It follows: “And do not harm the wine and oil.” Wine signifies the severity of the law; oil, the Gospel. The former intoxicates; the latter heals. The former unsettles the mind; the latter recalls the deranged to their right mind. “For the letter kills, but the spirit gives life” (2 Corinthians 3:6). These are harmed whenever they are wrongly understood. Whoever interprets the Scriptures badly, therefore, harms the wine and oil.

> [Note: Col. 0635D–0636D. Ten emperors are counted as persecutors of the Church down to Constantine the Great: first Nero; second Domitian; third Trajan; fourth Antoninus; fifth Septimius Severus; sixth Maximinus; seventh Decius; eighth Valerian; ninth Aurelian; tenth Diocletian with Maximian. These last, the cruellest of all, inflicted the greatest devastation upon the Church.]
>
> [Note: Col. 0636D. Vatican manuscript: “namely, to the kernel of that faith, etc.”]

And when he had opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth living creature saying: “Come and see.” Behold, after the third preaching of the third period, the fourth preaching follows, in which let us hear [Col. 0636B] what the prophet saw. “And behold,” he says, “a pale horse; and he who sat upon it, his name was Death, and Hell followed him. And authority was given to him over the four parts of the earth, to kill by sword, by famine, by death, and by the beasts of the earth.”

This horse—that is, the enemies of the Church—which first appeared red because of the blood of the martyrs and then black because of the wickedness of its life, is now seen as pale, since it was full of hatred, envy, and indignation. Moreover, it did not possess life, and whoever is deprived of life becomes pale. Hence it is added: “And he who sat upon it, his name was Death.” What other colour can that be upon which pale Death itself sits? In this place Death means the devil, who first brought death into the world. Thus Solomon says: [Col. 0636C] “Through the envy of the devil death entered into the world” (Wisdom 2:24). Hell follows him because Hell undoubtedly receives those whom the devil deceives and destroys. Thus, driven by a certain greed, Hell is said to follow this slaughterer and man of blood like a dog or a vulture. Hence the Psalmist: “Deliver my soul, O God, from the sword, and my only one from the hand of the dog” (Psalm 21:21).

Therefore authority was given to him over the four parts of the earth—that is, everywhere on earth, since this world is divided into four parts—to kill people by the sword, by famine, by death, and by the beasts of the earth: by the sword, indeed, of cunning persuasion; by famine, namely famine of hearing the word of God. “For this is he who takes the word from people’s hearts, lest, believing, they should be saved” (Luke 8:12); by death, whether tyrannical death or that by which souls are separated from God. Of this it is said: “For in death there is none who remembers you” (Psalm 6:6). By the beasts of the earth we understand evil spirits or heretics, concerning whom the Prophet says: “Do not deliver to the beasts the souls that confess you” (Psalm 73:19). These, indeed, rage more cruelly than all beasts.

> [Note: Col. 0636D. Some take this passage as a prophecy of the overthrow of the Roman Empire, which was to be entirely destroyed by sword, famine, pestilence, and other calamities. Thus Calmet.]

[Col. 0637A] And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw beneath the altar the souls of those killed for the word of God and for the testimony which they held; and they cried with a loud voice, saying: “How long, O holy and true God, will you not judge and avenge our blood upon those who dwell on the earth?”

For when the fifth preaching had begun, blessed John saw beneath the altar the souls of those who had been killed. Since they had been sacrificed for Christ, they are rightly said to be beneath the altar. The altar in this place may be understood as either faith or the cross. Hence the Apostle says: “But far be it from me to glory except in the cross of our Lord Jesus Christ!” (Galatians 6:14). But why had they been killed, except for the word of God which they preached and for the testimony of Christ which they possessed and bore? They cried [Col. 0637B] with a loud voice because God’s ears were open to their petitions. They asked the holy and true Lord, who has never lied to anyone, to judge them justly and to avenge their blood, unjustly shed by sinners. For they ask for nothing other than what they know he wills.

> [Note: Col. 0637D. Having set forth prophecies concerning the persecutors of the Church by whom the saints are to be killed, blessed John foretells the lot and happiness of those killed. He says that he saw their souls under the altar, that is, enjoying God in possession of eternal joy; and crying out for vengeance for the blood that they shed upon the earth. By this are indicated both the punishment of the persecutors and the end of their labours. Cornelius and Calmet collect here many further points concerning the state of souls after death; these are left to be read in their works.]

“And white robes were given to each of them, and they were told to rest yet a little while, until the number should be fulfilled of their fellow servants and brothers who were to be killed, as they also were.” Isaiah says of these: “They shall possess double things in the land” (Isaiah 61:7). They are double because their souls now enjoy blessedness with God, but afterward both souls and bodies shall receive immortality and glory. [Col. 0637C] Meanwhile, therefore, they have individual robes, because they have not yet attained the double portion. They wait yet a little while until the rest of the saints are killed in the final persecution to be carried out by Antichrist. Then at last, when the Lord comes for judgment, he will avenge them and give each one a reward according to his works.

> [Note: Col. 0637D–0638D. The vision of God, which the souls of the righteous attain immediately after their separation from their bodies, constitutes what theologians call their essential blessedness. Yet their happiness will not be complete and perfect until, after the universal resurrection, their bodies are united with their souls and their bodies are glorified; then they are said to receive the double robe.]

And I saw, when he had opened the sixth seal, and behold, a great earthquake occurred; and the sun became black like a sackcloth of hair, and the whole moon became like blood; and the stars of heaven fell upon the earth, as a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind; and heaven withdrew like a scroll being rolled up; and every mountain and island were moved from their places.

The sixth seal is the sixth preaching, which [Col. 0637D] we believe will be the last; in it Enoch [Col. 0638A] and Elijah are to come. Afterwards a sabbath-rest remains for the people of God. We shall have no need of preachers, because all things shall be naked and laid open. “For now we see through a mirror in an enigma, but then face to face” (1 Corinthians 13:12), when God will also be all in all.

Let us see, then, what shall take place in the final preaching. “And behold,” he says, “a great earthquake occurred.” Who can say how great then will be the earthquake, how great the disturbance of the people, how great the confusion of the Church and of the faithful, when Antichrist wars against the saints? “For then, as the Lord said, there will be such persecution as has not been from the beginning of the world” (Matthew 24:21). “And the sun became black like sackcloth of hair.” Concerning this sun it is written: “But for you righteous persons [Col. 0638B] the Sun of righteousness shall arise” (Malachi 4:2). It now shines in the Church, because we walk in its light; but then it shall be darkened by the preaching of the wicked, because he shall be proclaimed by the wicked as the Jews believe him to be. They shall call him a deceiver, deserving sackcloth and repentance; but Antichrist, who shall then appear, the Son of God.

Then the moon shall become like blood, because the holy Church shall be bloodied in complete martyrdom for Christ’s name. The stars of heaven shall fall lifeless to earth; or else, because many [Col. 0638D] who were thought faithful, shaken by terror, shall be separated from the Church.

> [Note: Col. 0638D. Vatican manuscript: “The stars of heaven shall fall upon the earth”; either because the saints will be slaughtered by persecutors and, literally, will fall lifeless upon the earth; or else because many, etc.] But how shall they fall? As a fig tree casts its unripe figs when shaken by a great wind. By *grossi* he means the first fruits of the fig tree, which readily fall when shaken by the wind. Heaven [Col. 0638C] shall withdraw like a scroll being rolled up, because, as many are separated from the faith through fear, the holy Church shall withdraw into itself, as it were, contract, and become smaller. But why like a rolled-up scroll? A rolled-up book conceals all that it contains. The Church is rightly compared to a rolled-up book, since, through excessive terror, it will not dare to preach at that time. Therefore, to strengthen it, 316 new and most renowned preachers will come—namely Enoch and Elijah.

It follows: “And every mountain and island were moved from their places.” After, he says, those signs which have been expounded above spiritually appear also literally in the sun, moon, and stars, it shall then be clear to all that heaven and earth are passing away and that the Lord will come suddenly to judge. Therefore every mountain and island [Col. 0639A] shall be moved from their places: that is, all the powerful persons of this age and all the nations of this world shall be converted from their former wickedness to the faith of Christ. “When the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, then Israel shall be saved” (Romans 11:55 [as printed]). This is what follows:

> [Note: Col. 0638D. What Christ the Lord warned the apostles would occur at the end of the world in Matthew 24 is here confirmed by John. Then there shall be a universal upheaval, when Enoch and Elijah oppose Antichrist as he rages and preaches against the truth. Yet, God permitting, deception shall prevail in many; righteousness shall seem, as it were, to be darkened like the sun; and the righteous, like stars, shall fall into corruption. Even the entire visible structure of the world shall be dissolved.]
>
> [Note: Col. 0638D. Vatican manuscript corrects the edition.]

“And the kings of the earth, and princes, and tribunes, and the rich and strong, and every slave and free person shall hide themselves in tombs and in the rocks of the mountains; and they shall say to the mountains and rocks: ‘Fall upon us and hide us from the face of him who sits upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb; for the great day of their wrath will come, and who can stand?’”

By the kings of the earth, princes, tribunes, rich, strong, and all slaves and free persons, all people without distinction are understood, who shall hide themselves in caves and rocks of the mountains. For what do the caves and rocks of the mountains mean except the saints, to whom all shall flee as to a tower, fortresses, and most strongly defended places, so that they may be protected by them? Then they shall say to the mountains and rocks—that is, to the aforesaid saints, whom they shall see standing securely without fear—that they may fall upon them, that is, conceal them. For thus we are accustomed to fall when, in order to help someone, we throw ourselves over him so that he may not be killed by another. But whence shall this great terror come, except from the face of him who sits upon the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb, whom they shall recognize to be angry together with his Father? Hence it is added: “For the great day of their wrath has come,” a day which indeed will have no end. “And who can stand?” No one, certainly, except one with whom he is not angry.

> [Note: Col. 0639D. This interpretation of Bruno’s is unusual. All commentators understand the matter literally: such and so great a terror and confusion from the signs preceding the coming of Christ the Judge will overwhelm people that they will suppose there is safety nowhere except in caves and dens; therefore they will eagerly seek them and hide in them.]

## CHAPTER VII

After these things I saw four angels standing upon the four corners of the earth, holding the four winds of the earth, lest the winds blow upon the earth, or upon the sea, or upon any tree. I think these angels are those of whom the Lord says: “The Son of Man will send his angels with a trumpet and great power, and he will gather his elect from the four winds” (Matthew 28:31 [as printed]). Likewise: “The angels will go out and separate the wicked from among the righteous and cast them into the furnace of fire.” And to these was given power to harm the earth, the sea, and the trees. But what is meant by the four winds except their power, which is to come with great [Col. 0639D] force? These winds are said to be held because, unless permitted, they cannot harm. They therefore restrain their power and strength until, at God’s command, they begin to blow. When they blow, what great disturbance will occur everywhere need not be stated. No one will be able to resist such a wind except one made pleasing by faith in the Trinity. Therefore the Psalmist says: “Not so the wicked, not so; but like dust which the wind casts from the face of the earth” (Psalm 1:4). But what is meant by the earth except sinners, who love only earthly and transient things? What by the sea except the unstable and fluctuating, who are carried about by every wind of doctrine? By the trees are understood those of whom the Lord says in the Gospel: “Every tree that does not bear good fruit shall be cut down and cast into the fire” (Matthew 7:19).

> [Note: Col. 0639D. It was stated beforehand in Wisdom 6 that God would arm every creature for vengeance upon his enemies and would make the world fight against the senseless; yet only when it pleased God. Therefore four angels are here said to have been appointed to restrain the four winds, lest with unbridled force they overthrow the earth. Other things, concerning which John’s following visions speak, had first to be fulfilled.]

And I saw another angel ascending from the rising of the sun, [Col. 0640B] having the seal of the living God; and he cried with a loud voice to the four angels, to whom it was given to harm the earth and the sea, saying: “Do not harm the earth, the sea, or the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God upon their foreheads.”

This angel, who is to announce prosperity and joy, is rightly described as coming from the rising of the sun. By his light, after the darkness of error has been driven away, he will separate the good from the evil. He shall have the seal of the living God, carrying, that is, the cross, which shall bring fear to the evil and joy to the good. And he cried to the four angels, namely the aforesaid hostile powers, to whom in their time permission had been granted to harm earth and sea; and he said: Restrain the winds; do not release the force and onset of your storm. Do not harm the earth, the sea, [Col. 0640C] or the trees, until we have sealed the servants of our God upon their foreheads, so that the tares may be gathered separately and the wheat separately.

This is the sign of the Trinity which we all received in baptism. They are said to need to be sealed again because this sign shall shine in each person’s forehead in such a way that no one shall doubt who is to be saved and counted among Christ’s servants.

> [Note: Col. 0640D. Most interpreters cited by Cornelius agree that this angel is Christ the Lord himself, called in Isaiah chapter 9 the Angel of Great Counsel and in Zechariah chapter 6 the Man, the Rising One; at his birth he caused peace to rise throughout the whole world. He ascended from the rising of the sun—that is, he rose in the morning—and immediately sent the apostles for the illumination of the world.]
>
> [Note: Col. 0640D. Vatican manuscript: “sealed again.”]
>
> [Note: Col. 0640D. “Those who have conformed to the symbol of the cross in faith and conduct will bear on their foreheads the certain sign of salvation. For Christ was crucified so that we might follow his footsteps, and perfect imitation of him will be the token of our election. We are sealed in baptism; we are sealed in confirmation; but works will make that sign life-giving and saving.” CORNELIUS.]

And I heard the number of those who had been sealed: one hundred and forty-four thousand sealed from every tribe of the children of Israel. For since there are twelve tribes and each contains twelve thousand, there is no doubt that this makes one hundred and forty-four thousand. But why he chose to assign twelve thousand to each tribe [Col. 0640D], I cannot know, unless perhaps because of the dignity of the number, which is found to be quite sacred in Holy Scripture [Col. 0641A]. I myself would believe that there will be more than these; nor do I think that as many will be saved from any one tribe as from the tribe of Judah, which always adhered to the Lord more than the rest.

> **Note: [Col. 0641D]** Writers hold various opinions concerning the number of Jews to be saved at the end of the world, as Cornelius reports; but more adhere to the authority of St Paul, who says, at Romans 11:26, that all Israel will be saved.

But since he had spoken of the children of the Church, whose multitude no one could number, he set the children of the Synagogue within a number, so that we may know that the children of the Church are far more numerous than these.

> **Note: [Col. 0641D]** Since, according to Christ’s promise, the whole world, before the end of the world, will become one flock under one shepherd, the number of Christians to be saved will be much greater than that of the Jews, who themselves will believe in Christ. Accordingly, as St Bruno rightly observes, their number is circumscribed by St John; [Col. 0642D] but of Christians he says that there is a great multitude which no one can number.

For what comparison is there between finite things and infinite? It follows: “From the tribe of Judah, twelve thousand sealed.” They are not placed here in the order in which the patriarchs were born; for Judah was not the firstborn, but Reuben was. But the latter, because he defiled his father’s bed, lost the rights of primogeniture; while the former, because Christ assumed flesh from his stock, received royal dignity. For Judah is interpreted “confessor,” and concerning confessors the Lord says [Col. 0641B]: “Whoever confesses me before men, I too will confess before my Father who is in heaven” (Matt. 10:32).

“From the tribe of Reuben, twelve thousand sealed.” Reuben is interpreted “seeing the son”; by him we understand those who, considering the works of the Father, recognize the Creator in created things.

“From the tribe of Gad, twelve thousand sealed.” Gad, who is called “girded,” signifies those to whom the Lord says: “Let your loins be girded, and lamps burning in your hands” (Luke 12:35). For such persons, always girded with the sword of God’s word, do not fear armies of vices or heretics.

“From the tribe of Asher, twelve thousand sealed.” For what do we understand by Asher, whose name is interpreted “blessed,” or “his bread is rich,” except those who, refreshing others with the richness of divine speech [Col. 0641C], lead them with themselves to the blessedness of eternal life?

“From the tribe of Naphtali, twelve thousand sealed.” Naphtali is interpreted “breadth”; by him we understand those who never depart from charity. For of charity it is said: “Your commandment is exceedingly broad” (Ps. 119:96). And likewise: “Love is the fulfilment of the law” (Rom. 13:10).

“From the tribe of Manasseh, twelve thousand sealed.” Manasseh is indeed interpreted “forgetfulness.” From his tribe are those who, made drunk with Christ’s cup, forget all earthly things. Such was blessed Paul, who said: “I judged that I knew nothing among you except Jesus Christ, and him crucified” (1 Cor. 2:2).

“From the tribe of Simeon, twelve thousand sealed.” But what does Simeon [Col. 0641D], who is interpreted “dwelling-place,” signify except those who pursue hospitality and say together with the Apostle: “We have here no continuing city, but seek the one to come” (Heb. 13:14), and with the Psalmist: “Lord, who shall dwell in your tabernacle?” [Col. 0642A] (Ps. 15:1).

“From the tribe of Levi, twelve thousand sealed.” Levi is called “addition,” and denotes those who never wish to be idle, but always labour and advance toward better things, daily adding something of virtue and goodness to themselves.

“From the tribe of Issachar, twelve thousand sealed.” Issachar, “a strong ass,” represents those of whom he says: “Bear one another’s burdens, and so fulfil the law of Christ” (Gal. 6:2).

“From the tribe of Zebulun, twelve thousand sealed.” Zebulun, who dwelt by the shore of the sea and devoted himself to sailing and fishing, denotes the ministers of the Church, who govern Christ’s ship—that is, the Church—and possess the ministry of baptism.

“From the tribe of Joseph, twelve thousand sealed.” Joseph is interpreted “increasing,” or “saviour of the world”; by him we understand the apostles and doctors [Col. 0642B], who caused Christ’s soldiery to increase and, sowing the word of God everywhere, saved the world, endangered by famine.

“From the tribe of Benjamin, twelve thousand sealed.” Benjamin, “a ravening wolf,” or “son of the right hand,” signifies those who are always eager for the word of God.

> **Note: [Col. 0642D]** Vatican manuscript: “to hear the word of God.”

They cannot be satisfied with the teaching of sacred speech; and these, leaving the left hand, walk by the right-hand way which leads to life. Such was the Apostle, who was born from the same tribe.

> **Note: [Col. 0642D]** By such interpretations of the tribal names, common among commentators, different paths to salvation are shown: namely, that some attain eternal life through excellence of faith, others through charity, others through contempt for the world, and others through the proclamation of the Gospel, and so forth.

That the tribe of Dan is not numbered among the other tribes, but that in its place the tribe of Manasseh—who was not Jacob’s son but Joseph’s—is inserted, I think signifies that, Judas having been cast out from the number of the apostles, Matthias was substituted in his place. For as Judas delivered Christ to death [Col. 0642C], so Antichrist, who is to be born from the tribe of Dan, by killing many of his servants will endeavour to destroy his name and faith.

After this I saw a great multitude, which no one could number, from all nations and tribes and peoples and languages, standing before the throne and in the sight of the Lamb, clothed in white robes, with palms in their hands. And they cried with a loud voice, saying: “Salvation to our God, and to him who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.” This great multitude, which is limitless and cannot be numbered, is the Church, gathered from every direction into one faith not from Jews alone, but from all nations, tribes, peoples, and languages.

Its children are said to stand before the throne because, as the Apostle says, “whether good or evil, we shall stand before the judgment-seat of Christ” [Col. 0642D] (Rom. 14:10). They also stood in the sight of the Lamb, because they were by no means among those of whom it is said: “Let the ungodly be taken away, lest they see the glory of God” (Isa. 26:10). But how did they stand? [Col. 0643A] Clothed in white robes: that is, clad in immortal and incorruptible flesh and made white by the garment of good works.

> **Note: [Col. 0643D]** The garment of the blessed in heaven, after they have received flesh in the resurrection, will be immortality, incorruptibility, and perfect glorification in every faculty, so that nothing may be lacking to their complete happiness.

“And palms in their hands”: by these it was signified that they had proved victorious over all their enemies. “And they cried with a loud voice, saying: Salvation to our God, who sits upon the throne, and to the Lamb.” Rightly they wish salvation to him and give thanks for salvation to him from whom they know that they have been saved.

> **Note: [Col. 0643D]** “Those,” says St Augustine, *Sermon 11 on the Saints*, “sing with a great voice who recall with great thanksgiving that they overcame the conflicts of assailing tribulations not by their own strength but with his assistance.”

And all the angels stood around the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures; and they fell before the throne upon their faces and worshipped the Lord, saying: “Amen. Blessing and glory and wisdom and thanksgiving, honour and power and strength, to our God for ever and ever. Amen.”

Concerning the throne, the elders, and the four living creatures enough has been said above. After the multitude of saints offered countless praises and thanksgivings to the Lord, the surrounding hosts of angels immediately answered their voice: they fell upon their faces and worshipped, saying, “Amen,” that is, “As you say, so may it be.” Let blessing from every creature, glory of nobility, wisdom in operation, thanksgiving for benefits, honour of dignity, power of rule, and strength to overcome enemies belong to our God for ever and ever.

> **Note: [Col. 0643D]** So long as we are in this world, clothed about with the veil of human weakness and ignorance, we cannot perform acts worthy of God’s praise and honour. But when we appear before his presence, [Col. 0644D] illuminated by the light of his countenance, then we shall be raised up to return thanks to him, magnify his goodness, and celebrate his other attributes, which we now know only in an enigma and in a mirror; but then we shall see and praise him face to face.

Amen.

And one of the elders answered and said to me: “Who are these, clothed in white robes, and whence have they come?” And I said to him: “My lord, you know.” And he said to me: “These are those who have come out of great tribulation and have washed their robes [Col. 0643C] and made them white in the blood of the Lamb. Therefore they are before the throne of God, and serve him day and night in his temple; and he who sits upon the throne dwells over them.”

Blessed John, in the person of the Church, was considering who those white-clad persons were whom he saw standing before the throne. He is therefore asked by one of the elders whom he supposes them to be, or whence they have come. Trusting not in his own judgment but wishing to hear the elder’s opinion, he answers that not he but the elder knows. For this is what all the elders preached; this is what they answer when questioned in the Holy Scriptures. Ask Paul, and he will tell you: “The sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be compared with the future glory which shall be revealed in us” (Rom. 8:18).

He therefore says: “These are those who have come [Col. 0643D] out of great tribulation,” which they endured for Christ’s name not only from persecutors, but also in hunger and thirst, cold and nakedness, and in many other ways [Col. 0644A]. “And they washed their robes and made them white in the blood of the Lamb.” A robe is a garment reaching to the ankles; by it we understand the flesh, redeemed by Christ’s blood and made whiter than snow. For this reason blood and water together came forth from Christ’s side: that he might redeem and wash us.

It follows: Those who have thus been washed and cleansed are therefore before God’s throne, where no unclean and defiled person can stand; and they serve him day and night, that is, without interruption, rejoicing and praising God in the heavenly Jerusalem. “And he who sits upon the throne dwells over them,” because they are subject to no other power: God alone is their ruler.

[Col. 0644B] “They shall hunger no more, neither thirst any more; neither shall the sun fall upon them, nor any heat; for the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne shall rule them and lead them to the fountains of the waters of life; and God shall wipe away every tear from their eyes.”

For those who are filled with the vision of the highest good cannot hunger or thirst. Neither will the sun fall upon them, nor any heat, because no scorching of tribulation and no burning of torments will thereafter descend upon them. Why is this? Because the Lamb who is in the midst of the throne—that is, the Son, who is in the bosom and heart of the Father—will rule them and lead them to the fountains of the waters of life. Refreshed by these, they suffer neither hunger nor thirst, neither heat nor burning. And God will wipe away every tear from their eyes, because nothing will be present on account of which they should weep and grieve [Col. 0644C]. For those who sow in tears will reap eternal life in joy.

## CHAPTER VIII

“And when he had opened the seventh seal, there was silence in heaven for about half an hour.” When the seventh seal was opened, there was silence.

> **Note: [Col. 0644D]** That a great mystery is contained in this silence is evident from the many interpretations reported by Cornelius. It is not for me to judge which of them has attained the truth. It is not improbable that it signifies the wonder and astonishment with which the inhabitants of heaven were carried away when, upon the opening of the seventh seal, they learned what would follow in the world before the last judgment, and what John afterwards announced.

For there will no longer be need for one person to speak to another: all will know all things. Then we shall see face to face him whom we now see through a mirror and in an enigma. But his saying, “for about half an hour,” has this force: although after the judgment no preaching will occur in the Church, he presents the silence as incomplete, because, beginning again from the start, he is about to speak of the same matters.

[Col. 0644D] Therefore he says: “When he had opened the seventh seal,” in which he revealed all secrets, “there was silence in heaven”—in itself continuous and eternal, but, for me, interrupted for half an hour because he was again to speak to the angels. And he began again to relate almost the same things he had said above, though in different words, as you will hear in what follows.

## THIRD BOOK

[Col. 0645]

[Col. 0645A] And I saw seven angels standing in the presence of God, and seven trumpets were given to them. Of these seven angels he will say nothing for the present, until he reaches the place where he says: “And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound the trumpet.” Meanwhile, let us see what follows.

And another angel came and stood before the altar, having a golden censer; and much incense was given to him, that he might offer it from the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar which is before the throne. And the smoke of the incense from the prayers of the saints ascended from the angel’s hand before the Lord.

For this Angel is Christ, who, receiving flesh from the Virgin, proclaimed the Father’s will to the world.

> **Note: [Col. 0645C]** Bruno expounded this mystically according to his custom. Yet there are those who maintain that an angel is signified truly and properly, like the seven others whom John mentions as sounding trumpets and pouring out bowls. For, as Arethas, Ribera, and others think, there is a particular [Col. 0645D] angel who stands beside the celebrating priest, helps and directs him, and offers his prayers and sacrifices to God—whether this is the guardian angel of the celebrant, or the guardian of the altar and temple, appointed particularly by God for this guardianship and the offering of sacrifices. Such an exposition plainly agrees with the prayer which we recite in the Canon of the Mass: “Humbly we beseech you, almighty God, command these things to be borne by the hands of your holy angel to your altar on high, in [Col. 0646C] the sight of your divine majesty.” Thus St Thomas, *Summa Theologiae*, III, question 83, article 4, reply to objection 9.

He stood before the altar because he did not fear to ascend the cross, upon which [Col. 0645B] he himself, both priest and sacrifice, offered himself to God the Father as a propitiatory victim for us. He had a golden censer, namely, the precious body which he received from the Virgin Mother, in which both divinity itself and the abundance of every virtue gave forth fragrance. “And much incense was given to him,” because the spices and prayers of the saints had little fragrance before they were placed in this censer. For he is the mediator between God and men, who presents our prayers to God the Father. Hence it adds: “That he might offer it from the prayers of all the saints upon the golden altar which is before the throne.”

Behold another altar, said to be golden, by which we understand God’s provident and most wise remembrance. Thus it seems to be said as if the aforesaid angel, with the golden censer, places the prayers of the saints from the altar of the cross upon the golden altar [Col. 0645C]. God’s remembrance is called an altar because no sacrifice is effective whose fragrance does not reach it. “And the smoke of the incense ascended”—“was made” is understood—from the prayers of the saints, from the hand of the angel who offered them before the Lord; for by the grace of the minister the offering was made acceptable.

And the angel took the censer, filled it with fire from the altar, and cast it upon the earth; and there were thunders [Col. 0646A], voices, lightnings, and a great earthquake. Above he had said that the angel having the golden censer stood before the altar; now he says that he took the censer itself and filled it with fire from the altar. We have said that the censer signifies Christ’s flesh and the altar the cross.

> **Note: [Col. 0646C]** Having adopted Bruno’s mystical interpretation of this passage, he diligently pursues it to the end, referring everything to Christ and the Church, [Col. 0646D] wherein his ingenuity is as worthy of notice as his piety. Other expositors, however, discuss at great length the plagues—indeed, the calamities—to be poured out upon the Roman Empire according to the differing periods. And truly, if events already accomplished are compared with these prophecies, we shall confess that they were true; and accordingly those things also must be held undoubted which will come upon the world when it approaches its end.
