He is also called Satan, because he opposes all truth and all justice; he deceives the whole world, for he deceives all who are deceived, and he was the origin of deception when the first human beings were placed in paradise. He himself was cast down, and his angels were sent with [Col. 0670D] him to earth; for when the devil fell from the heavenly places with all his host, he reigns and rules in those who are devoted to earthly pleasures and do not lift their hearts upward to God.

And I heard a great voice in heaven saying: “Now have come the salvation and the power and the kingdom of our God and the authority [Col. 0671A] of his Christ, because the accuser of our brethren has been cast down, who accused them before the presence of our God day and night. And they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb and by the word of their testimony, and they did not love their lives even unto death. Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them.” This voice is uttered and cried out daily both by the angels in heaven and by the saints in the Church; always giving thanks for such great benefits, they say: “Now salvation has come,” when the prince of death has been cast down and overcome; “and power,” because the devil has lost his power; “and the kingdom of our God,” because he who appeared to hold kingdom and dominion has been conquered and bound; “and the authority of his Christ,” for he is mighty—indeed almighty—to whom the Father said: “Ask of me, and I will give you the nations as your inheritance [Col. 0671B] and the ends of the earth as your possession” (Ps. II:8).

“Because the accuser of our brethren has been cast down, who accused them before the presence of our God day and night.” That the devil accuses the servants of God day and night, at every time and without interruption, may be understood from what is read concerning blessed Job, accused before the Lord by the devil:

> [Note: [Col. 0671D] The same manuscript: “accusing him, he speaks to the Lord, saying.”]

“Only stretch out your hand and touch all that he possesses, and see whether he will not bless you to your face” (Job I:11). He accuses us when, at his instigation, we do those things by which we offend God and become worthy of accusation. It follows: “And they conquered him by the blood of the Lamb.” For the blood of the Lamb, shed for our salvation, makes us victors over the devil.

> [Note: [Col. 0671D] Vatican manuscript: “For the saints gave testimony to the Lord and chose rather to die than to deny him for any love. And this is what is said: ‘And they did not love their lives even unto death.’ For ‘life,’” etc.]

> [Note: [Col. 0671D] Whenever any righteous person departs this life and is admitted into the heavenly homeland, he may exultingly say: ‘Now salvation has come to me through the power and might of Christ my God [Col. 0672D], the enemy and accuser, the devil, having been conquered. Redeemed by his blood and aided by powerful grace, I have overcome every enticement of the world and every fraud of the devil.’]

“And by the word [Col. 0671C] of their testimony, and because they did not love their lives even unto death.” That *anima* means “life” is found in the Gospel, where it is said: “He who loves his life shall lose it, and he who loses his life for my sake keeps it unto eternal life” (John XII:25). Thus in this passage also, “they did not love their lives”—that is, this present life—even unto death. For as long as they were in this life, through love of the other life they never loved this life. “Therefore rejoice, O heavens, and you who dwell in them.” For, as it is written: “There shall be joy in heaven before the angels of God over one sinner doing penance” (Luke XV:7). The angels rejoice at the conversion of the saints and are glad at their perfect manner of life.

[Col. 0671D] Woe to earth and sea, because the devil has come down to you in great wrath, knowing that he has little time. For seeing that he had been cast down from heaven and could have no fellowship with the saints, the devil came down to the earth and sea [Col. 0672A]—

> [Note: [Col. 0672D] Vatican manuscript: “Because among those he prepared for himself a place,” etc.]

—that is, to those among whom he prepared for himself a dwelling-place, whom he saw devoted to earthly desires and pleasures of the flesh. He also saw them tossing like the sea, carried about by every wind of doctrine. But woe to the wretched earth and unstable sea, because the devil, coming with great wrath and indignation, will crush and scatter everything. For he knows that he has little time; he does not doubt that he will suddenly lose his rule and dominion. Therefore he does harm now, who afterward will be unable to do harm.

And after the dragon saw that he had been cast to earth, he persecuted the woman who had borne the male child. And two wings of a great eagle were given to the woman, that she might fly into the wilderness, to her place, where she is fed for a time and times and half a time, away from the face [Col. 0672B] of the serpent. “For by the envy of the devil,” as the Apostle says, “death entered into the world” (Rom. V:12). Since he himself has been cast down, lost, and condemned, he therefore persecutes all and strives to cast down, destroy, and deceive all. But what need is there to say how, by what art, and by what devices he persecutes this woman, namely the holy Church?

The two wings of the great eagle given to the woman signify the two Testaments, or the two commandments of charity.

> [Note: [Col. 0672D] Most commentators agree in this interpretation, as Cornelius attests.]

The Church rightly received the eagle’s wings, which are swift and fly higher than all others; hence it is said of holy men: “They shall take up wings like eagles; they shall fly and not fail” (Isa. XL:31). On these wings the Church flies; with them she seeks the wilderness and secret places, where, devoting herself to divine contemplation [Col. 0672C] and persevering in the praises of God, she is not found by vices and malignant spirits. Hence it continues: “Where she is fed for a time and times and half a time, away from the face of the serpent.” A time signifies one year, times two years, and half a time half a year. The Church is rightly fed for so many years as Christ preached, because she is fed with that sole—

> [Note: [Col. 0672D] Vatican manuscript: “unique.”]

—and single food which Christ—

> [Note: [Col. 0672D] Vatican manuscript: “administered.”]

—preached during those years. For he himself says that he came not to be served, but to serve. How, and by whom, she is fed has already been said above.

And the serpent sent water from its mouth after the woman like a river, so that he might cause her to be swept away by the river; and the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and [Col. 0672D] swallowed up the river which the dragon had sent from its mouth. And the dragon was enraged against the woman, and went away to make war upon the rest of her seed, who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus; and he stood upon the sand of the sea.

The water which the serpent sent after the woman like a [Col. 0673A] river signifies either the foolish and erroneous learning of heretics, or also the persecutors of the Church. For such water proceeds from the mouth of the devil, and with such a river he strives to overwhelm Christ’s Church. Hence he says: *So that he might cause her to be swept away by the river.* For the Church is not carried away by the river, because she does not follow heretics. Even if she is at times dragged unwillingly to tortures by persecutors, she nevertheless does not yield to their command and will. The wicked, therefore, are swept away by this river; heretics drink this water and become intoxicated by it.

“And the earth helped the woman, and the earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon sent from his mouth.” What else is meant by the earth in this place but Christ’s humanity?

> [Note: Col. 0673D. Vatican MS.: “This earth of Christ helped the woman; it delivered the Church from the danger of death. It opened its mouth and swallowed up the river which the dragon sent from his mouth. For after Christ opened his mouth for preaching, a pattern of life,” etc.]

For this earth opened its mouth and swallowed up the river [336] [Col. 0673B] which the dragon sent from his mouth. After Christ opened his mouth for preaching, a pattern of life and rule of faith were given, by which all heresies are destroyed. At his command also rivers cease, sea and winds grow calm; there comes great peace and tranquillity, since, unless he permits it, the wicked do not dare rage against the good.

“And the dragon was enraged against the woman, and went away to make war with the rest of her seed, who keep the commandments of God and hold the testimony of Jesus.” The dragon is conquered, yet he does not rest; repulsed, he grows angry and is not ashamed; and what he cannot do to some, he attempts to do to others.

> [Note: Col. 0673D. How much Christians suffered under the Emperor Decius is abundantly clear from Eusebius, Book VI, chapter 41. They had rested for a little while, for the beginning of the reign of his successor Diocletian had been milder. But he soon became more savage and cruel, loosened every rein of ferocity against them, and put them to death with still more cruel tortures. Thus the devil appears conquered by the courage of the martyrs; yet, envying the Church’s glory, he sought to destroy her survivors, her children.]

He is separated from the mother and persecutes the children. Since he could not resist the leaders of the Church, from whom the rest derive their origin, he wages war against their children, whom he knows to possess God’s [Col. 0673C] commandments and testimonies; for he does not greatly concern himself with others. Hence it is written: “My son, when you come to the service of God, prepare your soul for temptation” (Ecclus. 2:1).

It follows: “And he stood upon the sand of the sea.” Fight bravely, saints of God, because you have been founded and made firm upon the solid rock. For your adversary stands upon the sand of the sea; if he is struck even lightly, he will immediately fall, since he has no foundation of stability whatsoever.

## CHAPTER XIII

“And I saw a beast rising out of the sea, having seven heads and ten horns; and upon its horns ten diadems, and upon its heads names of blasphemy.” What is meant by this beast except Antichrist? He is rightly called a beast [Col. 0673D] because, deprived of every humanity and rationality, [Col. 0674A] he will surpass all beasts in cruelty to such an extent that he will not fear to call himself the Creator of the world. This beast rises from the sea because, a son of bitterness and despair, he will arise from this stormy tempest of the world.

The seven heads signify his seven disciples; the ten horns will be ten kings, who will worship and adore him as God. Thus he is said to have ten diadems, which are the insignia of royal dignity. Names of blasphemy are mentioned upon his heads because the aforesaid sons of perdition will blaspheme God himself and dare, by perverse reasoning, to divide the Trinity itself.

“And the beast which I saw was like a leopard, and its feet were like the feet of a bear, and its mouth like the mouth of a lion; and the dragon gave [Col. 0674B] it his own power and great authority.” The leopard is an animal marked with a great variety of spots. This beast is therefore rightly said to resemble a leopard, because, faithless, unstable, and changeable in appearance, it lies to all and transforms itself into every form of deception.

“And its feet were like the feet of a bear.” Though they seem to have the likeness of a human foot, they nevertheless deceive those who follow behind them. Thus, when people arrive at the bear’s jaws, they realize that they have followed not a human being but a cruel beast. Hence it continues: “And its mouth was like the mouth of a lion.” Those whom it deceives either by variety of colours or by likeness of feet, it crushes and grinds down with a lion’s mouth. Thus it joins and subjects some to its company by the varied bloom of words, others by imitation of a false foot—that is, of a wicked work—and others by leonine rage and ferocity [Col. 0674C].

> [Note: Col. 0673D. Vatican MS.: “joins.”]

Therefore he adds: “And the dragon gave it his own power and great authority.” The malignant spirit will fill this son of perdition with his power and authority to such a degree that many will think him not a human being but God. Hence the Apostle says: “He who opposes and exalts himself above everything that is called God or is worshipped, so that he sits in the temple of God, showing himself as though he were God” (2 Thess. 2:4).

> [Note: Col. 0673D–0674D. This entire chapter appears to be a prophetic description of Antichrist, whose arts and cunning devices for deceiving humankind are set forth under the appearances of various beasts: now he is presented as a leopard, now as a bear, now as a lion. The dragon or demon is also said to have given him its own power and great authority, by which he will perform many things resembling wonders in order to deceive the nations, who will honour and fear him as God. Some think that, for greater deception, lest he seem to have anything unlike Christ, he will pretend to die and afterward appear as though raised from the dead; they explain thus the words: “And I saw one of his heads as though slain unto death, and the wound of its death was healed, and the whole earth marvelled.” See Cornelius. Others understand this of Julian the Apostate, in whom the beast—that is, the persecution which seemed to have been extinguished under the emperors Constantine and Constantius—revived in a sense with greater ferocity. So Calmet.]

“And I saw one of his heads as though slain unto death, and the wound of its death was healed; and the whole earth marvelled after the beast. And they worshipped the dragon who gave authority to the beast, and they worshipped the beast, saying: Who is like the beast? And who can [Col. 0674D] fight against it?” This may also be understood literally [Col. 0675A]: because he had heard of Christ’s death and resurrection, desiring to empty them of their power, he may pretend to perform in himself or in one of his disciples that which all marvel at as having been done in Christ.

> [Note: Col. 0675D. Vatican MS.: “He had heard of Christ’s death and resurrection; desiring to empty their power,” etc.]

Thus it says not “slain,” but “as though slain.” But if we understand it allegorically, one head slain unto death signifies that some heresiarch has fallen away. The wound of his death is healed because another succeeds in his place, one whose iniquity is so great that the death and wound of the former are consigned to oblivion. For unless they had seen some great and unprecedented sign, it would never be said that the whole earth marvelled after the beast.

“And they worshipped the dragon who gave authority to the beast.” First they worship the devil who is in him, as though he were some power and divinity; [Col. 0675B] then they worship and venerate this very son of divinity, whom they suppose to be full of omnipotence and divinity, saying: “Who is like the beast? Or who can fight against it?” For it raises even the dead and so swiftly bestows its own power upon anyone. It takes away from whom it wills, gives to whom it wills, the power of its divinity; and if it should perhaps be slain, the wound of its death is immediately healed.

> [Note: Col. 0675D. Vatican MS.: “they suppose, worship,” etc.]

“And there was given to it a mouth speaking great things and blasphemy; and authority was given to it to act for forty-two months. And it opened its mouth in blasphemies against God, to blaspheme his name and the tabernacle of his name, and those who dwell in heaven. And it was given to it to make war with the saints and to conquer them; and authority was given to it over every tribe and people and tongue and nation. And all who dwell upon the earth worshipped it, [Col. 0675C] whose names are not written in the book of life of the Lamb who was slain from the foundation of the world.”

“It was given,” he says, “to it by the prince of darkness, whom it will serve with all its powers, a mouth speaking great things”: a mouth speaking iniquity against God, a mouth speaking blasphemies, affirming that it alone is God.

> [Note: Col. 0675D. Vatican MS.: “blasphemy.”]

That it will reign for forty-two months we have often already said. It will blaspheme God, his Church, his servants, and his angels, preaching and declaring that all which we say the prophets spoke concerning Christ and his Church is false. Moreover, it will make war upon the saints, and will conquer temporarily not only others but even Enoch and Elijah themselves, and bring them to their completion in martyrdom. For authority is given to it over every tribe [Col. 0675D] of the children of Israel and over every people, whatever its language or nation. All who dwell upon the earth will worship and serve it: namely, all who are not predestined to life, whose names are not [Col. 0676A] written in the book of life, which the Lamb wrote and opened from the foundation of the world. He was indeed slain in order to free us from death and reveal to us the hidden things of heaven.

> [Note: Col. 0675D. Christ is said to have been slain from the foundation of the world not in actuality, but in types and figures, as in Abel, Isaac, and the patriarchs, who represented him.]

It follows:

“If anyone has ears, let him hear. He who leads into captivity goes into captivity. He who kills by the sword must himself be killed by the sword. Here is the patience and faith of the saints.”

If anyone, he says, has ears of the heart, if anyone has sound understanding, let him hear what has been said. Let him beware lest he be deceived by deceivers; let him know these things to be wholly true and never doubt that one who has led others into captivity, who by deceiving them has handed human souls over as captives to the devil, will himself go into captivity and be cast, bound hand and foot, into outer darkness. He who kills by the sword [Col. 0676B] must himself be killed by the sword, because one who destroys someone with the sword of deception—for deception too is a sword—will himself be slain by the sword of eternal condemnation.

> [Note: Col. 0675D–0676D. The Apostle exhorts the faithful to beware of Antichrist’s deceptions, because he and those seduced by him will be dragged down to Tartarus, condemned to everlasting fires. But those who patiently endure persecution will be rewarded with eternal joy.]

This, indeed, is the patience and faith of the saints: here it will be proved who is patient and faithful. For as gold is tested in fire, so the saint is tested in tribulation.

“And I saw another beast rising out of the earth, and it had two horns like a lamb, and spoke like a dragon. It exercised all the authority of the first beast in its presence, and caused the earth and those dwelling upon it to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound was healed.” This beast is perhaps that head which was said above to have been slain unto death. Therefore it [Col. 0676C] seems to rise from the earth, as though rising from burial, because the wound of its death was healed.

> [Note: Col. 0676D. Vatican MS.: “said.”]

> [Note: Col. 0676D. Again here Antichrist is designated under the likeness of a beast having two horns. He is said to have two horns, namely, the appearance and pretence of gentleness and holiness, in order to win for himself a following among people, who are easily ensnared by such things. Thus Cassiodorus, who adds that “Antichrist will perform so many miraculous signs that he will cause an idol to be worshipped with great devotion, though its falsity is discovered to be sacrilegious.”]

It is therefore said to have two horns like a lamb, so that it too might display in itself the figure and likeness of our Lamb who was slain and rose again. But because it spoke proudly, uttering poisonous words like a dragon, it is recognized not to have possessed the true innocence of the Lamb, although it imitated his appearance.

It exercised all the authority of the first beast in its presence because it was filled with the same spirit of iniquity, did not differ from it in miracles, and resembled it in falsehood.

“And it caused the earth and those dwelling upon it to worship the first beast, whose mortal wound had been healed.” [338] This may be punctuated so as to mean that this beast, whose [Col. 0676D] mortal wound had been healed, caused the earth and those dwelling upon it to worship the first beast. But if we understand the first beast itself also to have been slain and healed, this will not be unsuitable, since the whole is often taken for a part. [Col. 0677A] Therefore, when one of its heads is said to have been slain and healed, we may also say that it itself, in respect of that head, was slain and healed.

“And it performed great signs, even causing fire to come down from heaven to earth in the sight of men, and it deceives those dwelling upon the earth because of the signs which it was given to perform in the presence of the beast that had the wound of the sword.” Antichrist’s authority will be greater in this: not only he himself, but his disciples also will be commanded to perform many signs and wonders.

> [Note: Col. 0677D. Vatican MS.: “were seen.”]

> [Note: Col. 0677D–0678D. We have received this prediction from Christ in Matthew 24:24: “False Christs and false prophets will arise and give great signs and wonders, so that, if possible, even the elect may be led into error.” And in Mark 13:22: “They will give signs and portents to deceive, if possible, even the elect.” And Paul, speaking of Antichrist in 2 Thessalonians 2:9: “Whose coming is according to the working of Satan, in all power and signs and lying wonders, [Col. 0678D] and in all deception.”]

For just as magicians in Egypt performed many signs against Moses by their magical incantations, so these men will act against Enoch and Elijah. Hence they will also cause fire to descend from heaven.

> [Note: Col. 0678D. Vatican MS.: “For we read that Elijah once did this. Therefore they will deceive people all the more easily because they will seek not their own glory but that of their master.”]

And in this they will seek not their own glory but their master’s. For [Col. 0677B] though, by the miracles which they seem to perform, they could be worshipped if they wished, they will nevertheless command people to worship not themselves but Antichrist. They will strive to exalt his glory and magnificence so greatly that, after the manner of certain emperors, they will make wretched people worship even his statue and image. Hence it continues:

“And it was given to it to give breath to the image of the beast, so that the image of the beast might speak. And it caused all who did not worship the image of the beast to be killed; and it made all, small and great, rich and poor, free and slave, have the mark of the beast’s name or the testimony of its name.”

> [Note: Col. 0678D. We have supplied this from the Vatican codex.]

“It was given,” he says, “to it”—that is, to the devil—“it was permitted to give breath to the image of the beast.” A great and unprecedented miracle: that a statue of gold, silver, or [Col. 0677C] any other metal should seem to breathe and speak. “For, as the Lord says in the Gospel, false prophets will arise and give many signs and wonders” (Matt. 24:24).

By such signs they will thus attain the point that whoever refuses to worship the image of the beast will be killed by tyrants and rulers as profane and sacrilegious. Consequently, apart from the saints, who will not fear death, no one will be found, whether poor or rich, who does not have its mark and sign either on the right hand or on the forehead.

> [Note: Col. 0678D. Vatican MS.: “whether poor or rich.”]

For even to this day Scripture employs the first letter of a name in place of the whole name. Thus *character* (“mark”) is understood in place of “name,” and “name” in place of “faith.” Just as all Christians have the name—that is, the faith—of Christ impressed upon hand and forehead, so all servants and disciples of Antichrist will bear his name and faith either upon the right hand or upon the forehead.

A person bears the name and faith on the right hand when he does what he professes. When we see someone devoted to love, mercy, and piety, we do not doubt that he is a Christian; for his deeds themselves disclose who and what he is. If you wish to know him, attend not to the tongue but to the hand; for this is the Lord’s judgment: “You will know them by their fruits” (Matt. 7:16).

To bear the name and faith upon the forehead is to make them known to all and conceal neither one’s master nor one’s faith from anyone, so that, just as the forehead is open to all, so the faith may be manifest to all. Such terror, therefore, will seize everyone that no one will dare to do or say anything that appears to dissent from his faith. Hence it continues: “So that no one may be able to buy or sell unless he has the mark of the beast’s name, or the number of its name.”

For although this may be understood literally—as we frequently see done even by our own rulers, namely, that their letter and seals are carried for security’s sake—there is also [Col. 0678B] another, spiritual buying and selling, concerning which it is written: “She made linen cloth and sold it” (Prov. 31:24); and elsewhere: “All who thirst, come to the waters; buy wine and milk without silver and without any exchange” (Isa. 55:1).

Let such trading and such commerce take place in the Church: nothing is given there without a price; give faith and receive life. But this commerce will cease for the most part at that time, when it will be permitted to sell or buy the doctrines (*dogmata*) of his heresy only among heretics. Yet why should this be surprising in that greatest of all persecutions, when we read that even long ago emperors issued edicts that Christians, wherever they were found, should be punished without a hearing? It follows:

“Here is wisdom. Let him who has understanding calculate [Col. 0678C] the number of the beast, for it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.” Here, he says, wisdom is necessary: the things said are obscure and cannot be understood except by those with greater understanding.

> [Note: Col. 0678D. Vatican MS.: “understanding.”]

But whoever has understanding sufficient to attain knowledge of this matter should first calculate the number of the beast. Though it pretends to be God, it is not God but a human being; and this is what he says: “For it is the number of a man, and its number is six hundred and sixty-six.” By giving only the number six, he showed that it is human, since man was made on the sixth day. But because this six descends from ten, it signifies that he belongs to the tenth rank, so that he may be believed to be both human and devil, [Col. 0678D] not by nature but by iniquity. For ten times sixty makes six hundred.

> [Note: Col. 0678D. Vatican MS.: “Likewise, six times ten make sixty.”]

Let what the ancients have said suffice here. Adding nothing of our own, let us recall only what we have received from them. This book was published by blessed John in Greek [Col. 0679A] letters. It is clear that among the Greeks all letters express numbers. He therefore placed his name in the numerical value of letters, in order to exercise the reader’s understanding; it is as if he said: “The name in which this number, namely six hundred and sixty-six, is found—that is his name.”

For example, **ΑΝΤΕΜΟΣ**, which is interpreted “opposed” or “contrary”; from this Antichrist is called *Antichrist*, that is, “contrary to Christ.”

> [Note: Col. 0679D. Marchesius and the Lyons edition of the *Bibliotheca Patrum* read **ΑΝΤΕΜΟC**, but incorrectly. From the Vatican codex we have restored **ΑΝΤΕΜΟΣ**, so that the final letter of the word displays the sign Σ, which among the Greeks has the numerical value 200.]

> [Note: Col. 0679D. Vatican MS. writes in Latin letters: *Antemos*.]

You see, therefore, how well this name suits him, since it contains the whole number mentioned above in this manner: Α signifies one, Ν fifty, Τ three hundred, Ε five, Μ forty, Ο seventy, Σ two hundred; the total comes to 666. That is: Α, one; Ν, fifty; Τ, three hundred; Ε, five; Μ, forty; Ο, seventy; Σ, two hundred. Among the Greeks he is called **ΑΝΤΕΜΟΣ**, which among us is called Antichrist; and both mean the same.

There are also other names which appear to fit him by a certain correspondence of words. Since they contain the aforesaid number, they have been proposed by the ancients; yet no name suits Antichrist as aptly as the one just mentioned, **ΑΝΤΕΜΟΣ**. Nevertheless, to satisfy the reader, we shall give the other names also. They are **ΑΡΝΟΥΜΕ**, interpreted “I deny,” and **ΤΕΤΑΝ**, said to mean “sun”; and **ΓΕΝΣΗΡΙΚΟΣ**, understood as “deceiver of nations.”

> [Note: Col. 0679D. For these names see Calmet on this passage, who, in notes appended, explains the value of the letters in each name and, like our author, skilfully fits them to the number 666.]

How these names suit him the prudent reader readily understands. For brevity’s sake, we shall simply indicate the names and their numerical values. Α signifies one, Ρ one hundred, Ν fifty, Ο seventy; Γ four hundred, Μ forty, Ε five, Τ three hundred, Ε five, Ι ten, Τ three hundred, Α one, Ν fifty; Σ three, Ε five, Ν fifty, Σ two hundred, Η eight, Ρ one hundred, Ι ten, Κ twenty, Ο seventy, Σ two hundred.

Some also wished to express this name with Latin letters; but because this book was published in Greek, it does not seem very relevant. Yet we too shall give it, although it is useless: **DICLVX**. For among us D signifies five hundred, I one, C one hundred, L fifty, V five, and X ten; their total is six hundred and sixty-six. But what else does this seem to signify except that his flatterers, entreating him, will say: **DIC LUX**—“Speak, light; speak, lawgiver; do not be silent, you who are light; show us by what way we ought to walk.”

> [Note: Col. 0680D. Those who understand Diocletian to be this beast say that, in the name *Diocles Augustus*, the letters calculated according to Latin numeration make up the number 666. Calmet testifies, on Revelation chapter 13, no. 18, that this interpretation was approved also by Bossuet, bishop of Meaux, and seemed to him the most probable of all those adduced for this passage.]

But enough of these matters.

## CHAPTER XIV

“And I saw, and behold, the Lamb stood upon Mount Zion, [Col. 0680A] and with him one hundred and forty-four thousand, having his name and the name of his Father written on their foreheads.” Blessed John has related above how and where he saw Antichrist with all his army, and how all who had been seduced by him bore his name either on the right hand or on the forehead. Now he begins to tell of Christ and those who were with him: where he saw them and by what name they too were marked upon their foreheads.

“I saw,” he says, “and behold, the Lamb stood upon Mount Zion.” This is the Lamb of whom it is written: “Behold the Lamb of God; behold him who takes away the sins of the world” (John 1:29). He is rightly seen standing upon Mount Zion because, as King and Prince of the Church, he always helps her in every adversity. Hence he himself says: “But I have been appointed King by him over Zion, his holy mountain, proclaiming the commandment of the Lord” (Ps. 2:6).

He saw with him one hundred and forty-four thousand, by whom we understand the whole multitude of the Church. This number can be divided into twelve thousands, so that each of the twelve apostles has twelve thousand as his portion. Even if it is divided into its constituent parts, none of its parts lacks mystery.

For the number one hundred is perfect, and because the Lord willed it to be imperfect, he descended from heaven to complete it for the sake of one sheep. Hence he says: “What man among you, having a hundred sheep, if he loses one of them, does not leave the ninety-nine in the wilderness and go to seek the one that was lost?” (Luke 15:4).

The number forty belongs so fittingly to penitents that Moses, Elijah, and the Saviour of the world himself fasted for forty days; and Holy Church will imitate them every year until the end of the age. What need I say of the number four, which is everywhere most sacred because of the four Gospels and the same number of principal virtues? The number one thousand includes all; and although it is made up from other numbers, no number above it can be made from thousands.

Blessed John is therefore rightly described as seeing one hundred and forty-four thousand standing with the Lamb: through one hundred, the supreme perfection of virgins; through forty, all sinners converted to true repentance; through four, all observers of the [Col. 0680D] Gospels, who, like squared stones, remain always firm and steadfast in faith; and through thousands, the whole multitude of every sex, rank, condition, nation, and language.

> [Note: Col. 0680D–0682D. Cassiodorus briefly summarized this lengthy interpretation of Saint Bruno, saying: “He says that he saw the Lord Christ standing on Mount Zion, and with him 144,000 blessed persons, who bore on their foreheads the names both of Christ himself and of his Father written there. They were defiled by no lie and by no fornication against the faith; yet this clearly applies to all the blessed. These sang a new song to the Lord, which could not be sung by another; then they are praised in a remarkable exposition.”]

All these had his name and [Col. 0681A] the name of his Father written on their foreheads. But whose name is “his,” except that of the Lamb, and whose Father’s except the Father of the Lamb? For all were marked with the seal of the Trinity—namely, of Father, Son, and Holy Spirit. The Jews indeed have the Father’s name written upon their foreheads, but do not have the Son’s. We, however, have the name of both written upon our foreheads, because we praise and proclaim, believe and confess, both.

“And I heard a voice from heaven, like the voice of many waters and like the voice of great thunder; and the voice which I heard was like that of harpists playing upon their harps; and they sang as though a new song before the four living creatures and the elders.”

Since many waters signify many peoples, the voice of many waters is nothing other than the voice of many and diverse nations coming into one faith, praising and blessing God. The voice of great thunder is the voice of teachers preaching in the Church, of whom it is said: “Cry aloud; do not cease; raise your voice like a trumpet” (Isa. 58:1). Thus the one whose words these are is called in the Church a son of thunder.

“And the voice which I heard was like that of harpists playing upon their harps.” Because the praises and songs of the saints are sweet and sound pleasantly in God’s ears, their voices are therefore compared to harps. Such a harpist was David, whose song and melody soothed even demons. We still see this in the Church when, at a bishop’s exhortation, [Col. 0681C] adulterers, sacrilegious persons, murderers, and others filled with demons hasten to repentance.

They sing as though a new song because they expound the Scriptures of the Old Testament in such a way that they appear to speak something new. We may also understand the new song as the preaching of the New Testament. They are said to sing this before the four living creatures and the elders, and to stand as disciples before the faces of their teachers. The Church sings nothing other than what it has learned from these living creatures and elders.

“And no one could sing the song except those one hundred and forty-four thousand who were purchased from the earth. These are they who were not defiled with women, for they are virgins. These follow the Lamb wherever he goes. These were purchased from among human beings as firstfruits to God and to the Lamb; and no lie was found in their mouth, for they are without blemish before the throne of God.”

No one, he says, could sing and utter that song except those one hundred and forty-four thousand who were purchased from the earth. Neither Jew, pagan, nor heretic can sing that new and unprecedented song; for their old things have not yet passed away, nor have all things yet become new for them. The Church alone, therefore, [Col. 0682A] sings it; only those purchased from the earth, of whom the Apostle says: “For you were bought at a great price” (1 Cor. 6:20)—redeemed by Christ’s blood and raised from earth above the heavens—can sing this song there.

“These are they who were not defiled with women.” These are they who joined themselves not to prostitutes but to chaste wives. These women signify sects of heretics, whom holy men flee as foul prostitutes and with whom they wished to have no fellowship. Thus those who did not cleave to them are called virgins; these are called adulterers of the word of God. “For evil conversations corrupt good morals” (1 Cor. 15:33).

“These follow the Lamb wherever he goes,” as he himself says: “Father, [Col. 0682B] I desire that where I am, they also may be with me” (John 17:21). Therefore they will ascend into heaven, because the Lamb is there.

“These were purchased from among human beings, firstfruits to God and to the Lamb.” Just as a small portion of firstfruits from an abundant harvest is offered to God, so from all nations these few, in comparison with the wicked, are offered to God and the Lamb as certain firstfruits.

> [Note: Col. 0682D. Vatican MS.: “of the firstfruits.”]

“No lie was found in their mouth”: they could not be overcome by any tortures so as to deny the faith which they had once promised to God. Hence it continues: “For they are without blemish before the throne of God.” “For one who does not stumble in word is a perfect man” (James 3:2); “blemish,” however, is used for sin.

“And I saw another angel flying through the midst of [Col. 0682C] heaven, having an eternal Gospel to proclaim to those seated upon the earth, and to every nation, tribe, tongue, saying with a loud voice: Fear the Lord and give him honour, because the hour of his judgment has come; and worship him who made heaven and earth, sea and all things which are in them, and springs of waters.”

This angel signifies some teacher of the Church, because he sees that the hour of judgment and the unavoidable end of death approaches every person. Desiring all to be watchful and prudent, he diligently instructs them, ranging everywhere, concerning what they ought to do.

By the eternal Gospel we understand Christ’s preaching, which invites us not to temporal and passing goods but to eternal ones; which [Col. 0682D] was not composed by heretical invention but flowed from the fountain of eternal wisdom; and which speaks to great and small alike, saying: “Fear the Lord and give him honour, because the hour of his judgment has come,” so that he may render to each according to his works; “and worship him who made heaven and earth.” Worship and adore not demons, not Antichrist, but the Creator of all things.

And another angel followed, saying: “Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon, which made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication” [Col. 0683A]. This other angel signifies other teachers of the Church, who, the more nearly they perceive the day of judgment to approach, will daily devote themselves more earnestly to preaching, and will teach that all the glory and beauty of this world passes away and collapses, so that they may thereby tear human minds away from the desire for it. And this is what is said: “Fallen, fallen is that great Babylon.” For Babylon is interpreted “confusion,” and Nebuchadnezzar reigned in it; all Scripture attests that he bore the figure of the devil. Babylon therefore has fallen, because the world passes away, and its desire. For the form of this world passes away, and the whole confused multitude of the wicked will perish. But she made all nations drink of the wine of the wrath of her fornication [Col. 0683B], because all nations loved this present life so greatly that, corrupted in soul and body by its allurements, they did not fear to incur God’s wrath.

[Note: In the fall of Babylon—which was once a great city and the capital of the Chaldean empire—Rome is called by this name in Sacred Scripture, as at 1 Peter 5:13, and by the holy Fathers, on account of the likeness in corruption and the impious worship of false deities. According to some interpreters, her overthrow and the entire destruction of her empire are here foretold. But, in the manner of the prophets, that which is certainly to be done is treated as though already accomplished. We shall pursue this interpretation in chapter 17.]

And a third angel followed them, saying with a loud voice: “If anyone worships the beast and its image, and receives its mark on his forehead or upon his hand, he too shall drink of the wine of God’s wrath, mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of his wrath; and he shall be tormented with fire and sulphur in the sight of the holy angels and in the sight of the Lamb.” We understand this third angel to be the third and final preaching: when the saints see the abomination, and almost everyone turning to wickedness, and the beast and its image being worshipped, they will cry aloud and forbid so great [Col. 0683C] a crime to be committed; and they will declare to them what punishment awaits those who worship it, receive its mark, and drink of the wine of God’s wrath mixed with unmixed wine in the cup of his wrath.

This is the cup of which it is written: “For a cup is in the hand of the Lord, full of unmixed wine, mixed” (Ps. 74:9); by it we understand Sacred Scripture, which in itself is unmixed and pure, but is contaminated, troubled, and corrupted by heretics. Hence the Lord is said to be angry not with the cup, but with the wine of the heretics, which is mixed with unmixed wine and sound understanding. Those, therefore, who drink such wine and give their assent to the perversity of heretics will be tormented without end in eternal fire, which shall not be extinguished [Col. 0684A], and in sulphur of everlasting stench. This occurs in the sight of the holy angels and in the sight of the Lamb, because neither Christ nor his saints will ever forget those torments, according to the saying: “Remember, O Lord, the children of Edom in the day of Jerusalem” (Ps. 136:7).

“And the smoke of their torments shall ascend for ever and ever; and those who worship the beast and its image, and anyone who receives the mark of its name, shall have no rest day or night. Here is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus.” There the smoke rises perpetually; there the fire never fails. Therefore those whose torments do not cease to smoke will always be in the fire.

[Note: There was formerly an error of the Origenists, renewed by Abbot Joachim: that the punishments of the damned would not endure eternally, but that they would sometime be delivered from these torments. The Church condemned this error, since Sacred Scripture most clearly teaches the eternity of the punishments of hell.]

Concerning the beast, its image, and the mark of its name, enough has already been said above. But the words, “Here is the patience of the saints, who keep the commandments of God and the faith of Jesus,” [Col. 0684B] mean this: when the saints behold the torments of the wicked, they will then know that they have not endured patiently in vain, and that they have not kept God’s commandments and the faith of Jesus to no purpose.

[Note: This testimony plainly shows that faith alone is not sufficient for obtaining eternal salvation, as heretics contend; rather, good works are required—namely, the observance of the divine commandments.]

“And I heard a voice from heaven saying to me: Write: Blessed are the dead who die in the Lord. From now on,” says the Spirit, “let them rest from their labours, for their works follow them.” Once everything concerning the torments of the wicked has been completed—namely, that their suffering is eternal and that they will never have rest—the Lord pronounces judgment concerning the eternal blessedness [Col. 0684C] and rest of the good. He commands it to be written so that it may be believed firm and sure. “Blessed,” he says, “are the dead who die in the Lord.”

[Note: While a person still lives, no one can properly be called blessed; but after death he may be so called, because only in death is the consummation of righteousness and holiness accomplished. The prize is not received except at the finish of life’s course.]

But what is it to die in the Lord except to depart this life in faith, righteousness, charity, and firm hope, and, if necessary, to give one’s life for these things? “From now on,” says the Spirit—by whom this whole book is dictated and written—“let them rest from their labours,” which they have suffered, many and countless, for Christ’s name. “For their works follow them”: works worthy of remembrance, which will bear great testimony for them before the sight of the Lord.

## BOOK V

[Col. 0685]

[Col. 0685A] 343 “And I saw, and behold, a white cloud; and upon the cloud one seated like the Son of Man, having on his head a golden crown and in his hand a sharp sickle.” Blessed John, I say, saw a white cloud, by which we understand Holy Church: a cloud indeed because, by the rains of doctrine, it causes the hearts of many people, formerly dry, to put forth abundant fruits of good works; but white because, made whiter than snow, it is without spot or wrinkle. He also saw upon the cloud one like the Son of Man, namely Christ our Lord, who often used to call himself the Son of Man in the Gospel, according to the saying: “Whom do men say the Son of Man to be?” (Matt. 16:14). And he is rightly described as seated upon the cloud, over which he presides and rules as King and Lord [Col. 0685B] of the Church.

He has upon his head a golden crown, signifying that he is King and victor, adorned with every beauty. In his hand he has a sharp sickle, namely the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God; of it the Apostle again says: “For the word of God is living and effectual, and sharper than every two-edged sword” (Heb. 4:12). It should be noted that blessed John, beginning again from the head, as in the other books, sets forth what he has seen.

“And another angel came out of the temple, crying with a loud voice to him who sat upon the cloud: Send forth your sickle and reap, because the hour has come for reaping, because the harvest of the earth is dry. And he who sat upon the cloud sent forth his sickle, and the earth was reaped.” “Another angel,” he says, “came out of the temple” [Col. 0685C]. Another, certainly—and yet the same other: for he is God and man, though one and the same person, God and man. The angel therefore went out from the temple: Christ went out from the Father and came into the world. “The Lord is in his holy temple; the Lord, his seat is in heaven” (Ps. 10:4). He indeed went out from the temple and, at last, after much time, made himself known to men in signs and miracles.

“He cried with a loud voice to him who sat upon the cloud”: not because either one was deaf or the other could not otherwise be heard, but because God is said to cry with a loud voice to those who are prepared both to hear and obey his admonitions. The angel cried to the angel, God to man, divinity to humanity, when, through divine inspiration, Christ our Lord commanded, saying: “The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few. Pray therefore the Lord of the harvest, that he may send [Col. 0686A] labourers into his harvest” (Matt. 9:37).

[Note: Some interpreters, as Cornelius observes, prefer to understand not Christ here but an angel, because Christ is not called an angel but the Son of Man. This angel therefore goes forth to cooperate with Christ, and by Christ’s will and command to reap the ungodly, while Christ reaps the pious and holy.]

Christ therefore sent forth his sickle: he sent evangelical preaching through his disciples, and the earth was reaped, with wheat everywhere gathered into God’s granary, which is the Church.

[Note: Vatican manuscript: And likewise: “Lift up your eyes and look upon the regions, because they are already white for harvest. He therefore sent,” etc.]

“And another angel came out of the temple which is in heaven, having a sickle.” The comparison is the same as above, except only that there the good are gathered, whereas here the wicked are. For the angel who came out from the temple is Christ, who went forth as a bridegroom from the bridal chamber of the virginal womb. This temple is in heaven because she who was most blessed among all women so lived on earth that her manner of life was always in heaven. Indeed, already at that time—

[Note: Vatican manuscript: already then our Virgin.]

—our Virgin had departed this life and had been exalted above the choirs of angels [Col. 0686B] when blessed John wrote these things.

[Note: Bruno reports that in his day the opinion was commonly accepted in the Church that the Blessed Virgin Mary, after her death, was exalted or assumed into heaven; St Bernard adorned this belief with very many praises.]

John therefore saw the angel who had come out of the temple when the temple had long since been transferred to heaven. Like the former angel, he had a sharp sickle; this has been explained above. It follows:

“And another angel came out from the altar, who had power over fire; and he cried with a loud voice to him who had the sharp sickle, saying: Send forth your sharp sickle and gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because its grapes are now ripe.” As by the temple we understand the Virgin’s womb, so by the altar we understand the Lord’s body. For he taught that he himself was the altar when, with his own hands, he offered that greatest sacrifice to his disciples, saying: 344 “Take and eat, [Col. 0686C] this is my body” (Matt. 26:26). The angel therefore came out from the altar when God deigned to reveal himself to men in man.

This angel has power over fire, because no one is kindled with the fire of the Holy Spirit except by his gift. Hence he himself says: “I came to send fire upon the earth; and what do I will but that it burn?” (Luke 12:49). And this angel rightly commanded him who had the sharp sickle to gather the clusters of the vine of the earth, because the assumed man did nothing except by the counsel of divinity.

It should be known that there are two vines: one of the good and the other of the wicked. Concerning the vine of the good it is written: “The kingdom of heaven is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire labourers for his vineyard” (Matt. 20:1). [Col. 0686D] But the vine of the wicked is that of which we are now speaking. It is therefore rightly called the vine of the earth, whose first vine was Ham. This vine is gathered daily, since the wicked are daily taken from this life.

[Note: St John distinguishes two orders of men: the righteous and the reprobate. The lot of the former is happy and most blessed, because Christ will bring them into his own portion and establish them in his kingdom as heirs and possessors of eternal blessedness. But the reprobate will be cast by the angels, ministers of God’s wrath, as perpetual exiles from the heavenly city, into the lake of fire.]

Thus it continues:

“And the angel sent his sickle into the earth, and gathered the vine of the earth, and cast it into the great lake of God’s wrath; and the lake was trodden outside the city, and blood came out from the lake as high as horses’ bridles, for one thousand six hundred stadia.” By the sickle in this place we understand Christ’s command and the ministers of his vengeance. He sends it daily into the earth, and does not cease to gather the vine of the earth; for the wicked, filled and hardened in their iniquity, are suddenly cut off from vine and life together, when it is least expected. Once cut off, they are not cast into any ordinary winepress, but plunged into the great lake of God’s wrath, which is hell.

[Col. 0687B] “And the lake was trodden outside the city, and blood came out from the lake.” This lake is not contained within the holy city; it is outside, and outside it is trodden, with evil spirits as its treaders and vine-dressers. Abraham signified that it was outside the city when he said: “Between us and you a great chasm has been established. And blood came out from the lake as high as horses’ bridles for one thousand six hundred stadia” (Luke 16:16). This mode of speech is called hyperbole by grammarians. When we wish to indicate that a great battle has occurred somewhere, we commonly say that so much blood was poured out there that horses swam in the blood. Likewise, in this passage blessed John, wishing to signify divine vengeance, the punishment and death of the wicked, says that their blood rose as high as horses’ [Col. 0687C] bridles. Another prophet explains this more expressively: “And the saints shall go out and see the corpses of the dead who transgressed against me, and they shall be until every flesh is sated with the sight” (Isa. 66:24). What is there “until every flesh is sated with the sight” is here “as high as horses’ bridles.”

But what else is it for blood to come out from the lake except for the punishment and torments of the wicked to become known to the people of this world? Hence it is said to have come out for one thousand six hundred stadia. By the thousand stadia we understand the whole extent of the world, but by the six hundred are signified the six ages.

[Note: Vatican manuscript: are figured.]

And all things are rightly understood by the thousand, since, as we have already said, all numbers are contained in a thousand. Blood therefore came out for a thousand stadia because there is nowhere [Col. 0687D] where the punishment of the wicked has not been heard of; it came out for six hundred stadia because there was no age in which the same had not been revealed.

[Note: The fable of Sisyphus does not allow one to doubt that the eternity of infernal punishments was known even to the pagans.]

That a stadium denotes not merely an earthly measurement but also a length [Col. 0688A] of time, hear the Apostle saying: “Do you not know that those who run in the stadium all indeed run, but one receives the prize?” (1 Cor. 9:24). Explaining this elsewhere, he says: “I have fought the good fight; I have finished the course; I have kept the faith” (2 Tim. 9:7): namely, the course of the stadium of this present life.

## CHAPTER XV

“And I saw another sign in heaven, great and marvellous: seven angels having the seven last plagues, because in them the wrath of God is completed. And I saw as it were a glassy sea mixed with fire, and those who overcame the beast, its image, and the number of its name, standing upon the glassy sea, having the harps of God and singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song [Col. 0688B] of the Lamb, saying: Great and marvellous are your works, O Lord God Almighty.”

“I saw,” he says, “a great and marvellous sign in the Church: seven angels, that is, seven orders of teachers succeeding one another at different times, having the seven last plagues.”

[Note: These are regarded as forewarnings of those calamities to be poured out upon the ungodly, and, according to some, especially upon the Roman Empire which is to be utterly overthrown. They will be poured out by the angels at the appointed time, and the prophecies concerning them belong to the following chapter.]

But why “last”? 345 Because in them the wrath of God is completed. For those plagues will be so great and immense that God’s wrath can be completed and satisfied by them. “Last” is sometimes used for final, sometimes for worse. We shall say much concerning these plagues in what follows.

“And I saw as it were a glassy sea mixed with fire.” The glassy sea is the water of baptism, wholly mingled and sanctified with the fire of the Holy Spirit. Of this John, the Forerunner of the Lord, said [Col. 0688C]: “I baptize you in water; but he who comes after me is stronger than I, whose sandals I am not worthy to untie; he will baptize you in the Holy Spirit and fire” (John 1:26). There is therefore a glassy sea mixed with fire, so that the sanctified water, glass-like and pure, may wash bodies outwardly, while the fire of the Holy Spirit may burn away vices inwardly and cleanse man from sin.

“And I saw those standing upon the glassy sea who overcame the beast, its image, and the number of its name.”

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “And I saw those who overcame the beast, its image, and the number of its name, standing upon the glassy sea. For much has been said above about the beast, its greatness, and the number of its name. But it is not enough to stand upon the glassy sea; it is not enough to have been regenerated by the water of baptism,” etc.]

It is not enough to have been regenerated by the water of baptism unless, in addition, we overcome and despise the beast, its image, and the number of its name. But you say: How can I overcome that beast which has not yet come? Hear what blessed John also says in his Epistle: “My little children, it is the last hour; and as you heard that Antichrist is coming, even now there are many antichrists” (1 John 2:18). Thus, although at the end of the age that son of perdition and head of all the wicked is to come, [Col. 0689A] nevertheless he daily sends ahead his members, in whom indeed he is overcome by the faithful.

[Note: Up to the present, in the sense of St John the Apostle, there have been many antichrists in the Church, and they will continue until the world’s end. But as those earlier ones, whether heretics or tyrants, were unable to withstand God’s truth and power, so these latter ones will be destroyed. Hence there will be very great joy in the Church over their downfall.]

For everyone who contradicts Christ is an antichrist. Therefore he who stands upon the glassy sea, who fishes and swims in baptism, must overcome the beast and its image—must overcome Antichrist and his disciples, who are conformed and similar to him. Nor must he receive—

[Note: From the Vatican manuscript we have thus corrected the text. The edition reads: “it may suffice.”]

—the number of its name, that is, its faith and doctrine. But what were these doing upon the sea? It follows: “Having the harps of God and singing the song of Moses, the servant of God, and the song of the Lamb.” The harp of God is the melody of divine inspiration, concerning which the Lord himself said to his disciples: “For it is not you who speak, but the Spirit of your Father who speaks in you” (Matt. 10:20). By the song of Moses and the song [Col. 0689B] of the Lamb we understand the Old and New Testaments.

Therefore all who stand upon the glassy sea, all who invite others to the sacrament of baptism, should thus play the harp and sing in this manner and of these things: “Great and marvellous are your works, O Lord God Almighty; just and true are your ways, King of the ages. Who shall not fear you, O Lord, and magnify your name? For you alone are holy; for all nations shall come and worship before you, because your judgments are manifest.” What then does it mean that “your judgments are manifest,” when elsewhere it is written: “Your judgments are a great abyss” (Ps. 35:7)? God’s judgments are both manifest and hidden: hidden, because no one is able fully to disclose them; manifest, because, however they come about, [Col. 0689C] no one nevertheless doubts that they are just and true.

The teachers standing upon the glassy sea, seeing the Gentiles who were without God hastening to baptism, but the Jews, who possessed the Law and had been justly condemned by God, not seeking the medicine of salvation, are astonished at the works of the Lord and marvel. Although they do not know why the former are chosen and the latter rejected, they nevertheless say that God’s ways are upright and just. Therefore they preach that God should all the more be feared and magnified, because in mercy and compassion alone he calls the Gentiles, while he confounds and condemns the pride of the Jews.

“And after these things I saw, and behold, heaven was opened: the temple of the tabernacle of testimony in heaven; and seven [Col. 0689D] angels came out from the temple, having the seven plagues, clothed in clean and white linen and girded about the breasts with golden girdles.” The temple of the tabernacle of testimony was then opened in heaven when Christ’s preaching first resounded in the Church through the mouths of the Apostles. For the Apostles are the temple, bearing and preaching in the sanctuary of their breast the very tabernacle and all the written testimonies of the Law and the Prophets.

[Col. 0690A] Seven angels having plagues came out from this temple because all orders of teachers, deriving their origin from the Apostles, immediately preach in the Church in their respective times what they learned from them. And because, as the Apostle says, “To some they are the savour of life unto life, to others the savour of death unto death” (2 Cor. 2:16), they bring plagues upon those who do not obey their admonitions.

They are clothed in clean and white linen: namely, that precious pearl of which the Lord speaks in the Gospel, saying: “The kingdom of 346 heaven is like a merchant seeking good pearls; when he found one precious pearl, he gave all that he had and bought it” (Matt. 13:45–46). By it we understand Christ’s faith and ecclesiastical doctrine [Col. 0690B]; whoever is not clothed with it will not dare recline among Christ’s guests. They are girded about the breasts with golden girdles, so that from what outwardly appears it may be understood how great a treasure of wisdom and knowledge lies hidden inwardly in their hearts.

“And one of the four living creatures gave to the seven angels seven golden bowls, full of the wrath of God, who lives for ever and ever. And the temple was filled with smoke from the majesty of God and from his power, and no one could enter the temple until the seven plagues of the seven angels were completed.” There are four living creatures, yet all tell and say one and the same thing, because they describe Christ’s preaching alone. Therefore what one of them gives is undoubtedly given by all.

But what does it mean that the seven angels are said to have been given seven golden bowls full of the wrath of the living God, except that all teachers of the Church received the doctrine which they possess and preach? Although this doctrine is golden and seasoned with the salt of wisdom, it is eagerly received by some but rejected by others as something tasteless and without savour. Upon those who reject it they pour down God’s indignation and wrath.

[Note: These words may be referred to what Christ the Lord said to the Jews in John 8:47: “He who is of God hears God’s words; therefore you do not hear, because you are not of God”; and consequently they fell into dreadful hardening.]

Because of such persons, therefore, these golden bowls, although they contain every delight, are nevertheless said to be full of the wrath of the living God. The temple filled with smoke from God’s majesty and power can be understood either as Holy Church or as [Col. 0690D] the heavenly Jerusalem. God’s power and majesty, which always dwell in the Church, by a certain divine and hidden judgment blind the minds of unbelievers so that they may neither be converted to the faith nor enter the Church. Hence the Apostle says: “The natural man does not receive the things which are of the Spirit of God; for neither can he, because they are spiritually discerned” (1 Cor. 2:14). This is what is meant by: “And no one could enter [Col. 0691A] the temple until the seven plagues were completed.” For when these have been completed, there will be a greater entrance into the Church. For “when the fullness of the Gentiles has entered, then Israel shall be saved” (Rom. 11:25).

But concerning the heavenly Jerusalem it is certainly known that no one enters it bodily until, when these seven plagues are ended, the saints rise to immortality. It is rightly said to be full of the smoke of spices and incense, proceeding from the prayers of the saints, because where God’s majesty and power are, there the prayers and devotions of the saints are directed.

## CHAPTER XVI

“And I heard a great voice from the temple saying to the seven angels: Go and pour out the seven bowls of God’s wrath upon the earth. And the first went and poured out his bowl [Col. 0691B] upon the earth, and there came a grievous and most evil sore upon the people who had the mark of the beast and upon those who worshipped its image.”

[Note: Those who maintain that this chapter should not, like our commentator, yield moral senses but should be understood as prophecies of the overthrow of the Roman Empire take the great voice to mean God’s will made known to John. When the time had come for establishing the new law, God determined to overthrow the Roman kingdom because it would act more harshly against the religion of the true God. These interpreters therefore begin to count the plagues, or scourges, inflicted at different times from Valerian, who, defeated by Sapor king of the Persians, endured miserable captivity and a still more cruel death. For it is certain that Rome, made the sport of barbarian rulers, was devastated not so much by wars as by plagues, famine, earthquakes, fires, and diverse kinds of ravaging. Thus Cornelius, Calmet, Bossuet, Sassi, and others.]

This great voice is daily heard in God’s temple, which is the Church. For what else do the Gospels proclaim except that teachers should go out to evangelize and openly declare to all how much wrath and indignation will come upon sinners unless they repent? When the saints announce future punishment, what else do they do but pour out upon the earth bowls full of God’s wrath? Hence it follows: “And the first went and poured out his bowl [Col. 0691C] upon the earth.” The first angel is the first order of preachers, which then poured its bowl upon the earth when it announced to the primitive Church not only the grace prepared for the good but also the torments awaiting sinners. The Apostle poured out this bowl when he said that “the Lord will render to each according to his works: to those indeed who by patience in good work seek glory, honour, and incorruption; but upon those who are contentious and do not obey truth but believe in iniquity shall come wrath and indignation, tribulation and distress” (Rom. 2:6, 10).

It follows: “And there came a grievous and most evil sore upon the people who had the mark of the beast and upon those who worshipped its image.” The beast has not yet been born, and already wretched 347 people venerate its mark and name, and worship its image and likeness. [Col. 0691D] Its image was Simon Magus, Arius, and the other sons of the devil. The Jews venerate its image and mark, confessing that they still await the Messiah. Upon these came a grievous and most evil sore, which certainly cannot be healed.

[Col. 0692A] “If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have sin; but now they have no excuse for their sins” (John 15:21). What then? Did Christ’s preaching wound them and make them sin? Far be it. Rather, when Christ preached and they would not receive his admonitions, they were wounded and slain by the devil, and enrolled in his service. Hence the Apostle says: “For sin, taking occasion by the commandment, deceived me and by it killed me” (Rom. 7:11). Thus, while the Apostles preached, when the Jews and the others who had been seduced into error would not receive their words, they were so grievously wounded by the devil that they could no longer be healed.

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “may not be able.”]

“And the second poured out his bowl upon the sea, and it became blood like that of a dead man, and every living soul died in the sea.” The second angel poured out his bowl upon this great and spacious sea [Col. 0692B] when the second order of preachers began to rebuke the armed wisdom of this world, the doctrine of philosophers and heretics, and also the false worship of gods.

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “poured out.”]

Hence it follows: “All the water of the sea was turned into blood, and that blood was [the blood] of a dead man. And every living soul died in the sea.”

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “And all that blood became black and stinking, like the blood of a dead man. And every soul,” etc.]

For the more true doctrine is made clear, the more false knowledge is turned into blood and sin. The person who follows falsehood after knowing the truth sins more than one who has never heard the voice of truth. The sea is therefore rightly turned into blood, and kills and destroys those who drink it [Col. 0692C], when thirsting people ought to run not to the sea, but to the bowl of sound faith poured out over them.

“And the third poured out his bowl upon the rivers and the fountains of waters, and they became blood.” What do we understand by rivers and fountains of waters except the books of the Law and the Prophets? The teachers of the Church poured out upon these their bowl—that is, spiritual interpretation—so that they might no longer be understood according to the letter; “for the letter kills, but the Spirit gives life” (2 Cor. 3:6). It kills indeed when it is changed into blood, from which it even commands its observers to abstain. These fountains, formerly drinkable when understood according to history, [Col. 0692D] now make men heretics unless they are understood spiritually. Let those who delight in such knowledge therefore know that they drink not water but blood.

“And I heard the angel of the waters saying: You are just, [Col. 0693A] who are and who were, the Holy One, because you have judged these things; for they poured out the blood of saints and prophets, and you have given them blood to drink: for they are worthy. And I heard another from the altar saying: Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are your judgments.”

The fourth preacher praises the words of the teachers before him and furthermore gives thanks to God because he has permitted wicked and proud people, who preferred to believe and imitate the foolish wisdom of heretics and philosophers rather than true and catholic faith, to remain in their folly and error. To confirm this, the entire ecclesiastical multitude which does not depart from the altar of right faith answers: “Yes, Lord God Almighty, true and just are your judgments.” You see how great is the harmony in the people of God, and how all holy preachers answer one another in turn and with one voice proclaim and exalt God’s works and righteous judgments. It follows:

“And the fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the sun, and it was given him to afflict people with heat and fire. And people were scorched with great heat, and they blasphemed the name of God, who has power over these plagues; and they did not repent to give him glory.” After the fourth angel had praised God’s judgments, he too, unwilling that his bowl should be idle, poured it out upon the sun. By the sun in this place we understand one who, though blind and wrapped in the darkness of every obscurity—

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “enveloped round about.”]

—will nevertheless not fear to call himself God and the sun of righteousness. This man, unable to endure sound doctrine and bearing heavily the bowl poured out upon him [Col. 0693C]—

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “poured out over himself.”]

—because he has nothing with which he can answer the teachers of the Church, will become angry and indignant with his own people. As is the manner of unbelievers, he will call them base and contemptible if they do not avenge his injuries.

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “if they do not promptly judge [them].”]

Thus he will heat and provoke them to such madness that they will dare to blaspheme not only the saints but even the Creator of the world.

[Note: Such are those impious persons who condemn God’s providence and dispute concerning his existence; if not in words, they are certainly proved atheists by their deeds.]

And this is what is said: “It was given him to afflict people with heat and fire, and people were scorched with great heat.” For we very often see people afflicted and scorched by such heat and fire when, stirred by such wrath at the devil’s instigation, scarcely one man can be restrained by many from rushing, wholly pale and disturbed, like a beast, into [Col. 0693D] bloodshed—to the crime he had conceived in his mind.

It follows: “And they blasphemed the name of the Lord, who has power over these plagues, and they did not repent to give him glory.” You see therefore what the devil’s goad, what the dragon’s tail, what the son of iniquity works in those who obey him—

[Note: Vatican manuscript: “works.”]

—with what fire he kindles them, with what heat he inflames them, and with what goads he drives them.

And the fifth angel poured out his bowl upon the throne of the beast, and his kingdom became dark; and they gnawed their tongues because of pain, and blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and their wounds, and did not repent of their deeds. The fourth angel poured out his bowl upon the beast itself, which he also called the sun; but the fifth is said to have poured out his bowl upon the beast’s throne. By this we understand its greater and stronger members—namely, the leaders of heresies and tyrants.  
[Note: Codex Vaticanus: “But the fifth is said to have poured out his bowl upon the beast’s throne. The beast’s throne is greater and stronger,” etc.] Upon these teachers pour out their bowls when, recalling to their memory their sins and errors, they set forth in order what punishments and torments they will suffer for them. Thus those who ought, if they had God favourable to them, to have been enlightened by such words, instead become obstinate against the truth, darkened and blind. And this is what is said: “And his kingdom became dark.”

It follows: “And they gnawed their tongues because of pain, and blasphemed the God of heaven because of their pains and wounds, and did not repent of their deeds.” Behold: those who, wisely admonished, ought to have turned to repentance and tears, were so stirred to anger and indignation by the words of the saints, as though grievously wounded by certain missiles, that they both blasphemed the Lord and, grinding their teeth among themselves like madmen, gave no thought to what they said. For this is what he means when he says: “They gnawed their tongues because of pain.” What else is it to gnaw one’s tongue because of pain than to speak thoughtlessly and irrationally? It follows:

And the sixth angel poured out his bowl upon that great river Euphrates, and its water dried up, so that the way might be prepared for the kings from the rising of the sun. For the great river Euphrates, which is divided into many parts, signifies heretics, who are divided into manifold and diverse sects. The angel poured the bowl of his preaching upon these; he dried up their waters, springs, and streams, and for the most part destroyed their heresies. Thus, when the water that had impeded them was dried up, the way was prepared for kings coming from the rising of the sun. The saints are called kings because, knowing how to govern themselves wisely, they allow no vice to hold dominion in them. Hence the Apostle says: “Let not sin reign in your mortal body” (Rom. 6:12). They come from the rising of the sun because light always goes before them. They know no setting; but, advancing from virtue to virtue, as from light to light, they always gaze upon the rays of the sun like eagles.

And I saw, from the mouth of the dragon, from the mouth of the beast, and from the mouth of the false prophet, three unclean spirits like frogs. For they are spirits of demons, working signs; and they go out to the kings of the whole earth, to gather them for battle on the great day of God Almighty—he is understood to be saying: “Behold, I come like a thief. Blessed is he who watches and keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame”—and he shall gather them into the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.

For Antichrist is called a dragon because of his strength and agility in deceiving; he is also called a beast because of his cruelty; and he is called a false prophet because he falsely claims to be Christ. From his mouth, he says, three unclean spirits go forth; explaining them immediately afterwards, he acknowledges that they are spirits of demons. Endowed with such a trinity of demons, he will enrich all his disciples with the false power of signs and wonders. They are rightly said to resemble frogs, because they fill with chatter, uncleanness, and every sort of filth those whom they corrupt by their loquacity. These go out to the kings of the whole earth—not, certainly, to those for whom the way from the rising of the sun is prepared, but rather to those who love only earthly and transitory things, honours and dignities. But why do they go out? It follows: “To gather them for battle on the great day of the Almighty.”

Yes indeed, devil: this is how you love your own; this is your counsel, to persuade them to fight against him whom neither you nor they will be able to resist.  
[Note: Codex Vaticanus: “nor will they themselves be able to resist.”]  
[Note: Codex Vaticanus: “You indeed do all this,” etc.]  
You do this so that you may be condemned in judgement not alone, but with many. But you, saints, beware lest you be deceived; for the Lord himself says to you: “Behold, I come like a thief,” while all people are ignorant of my coming. Blessed therefore is he who watches—and watches always—lest he be overtaken unawares; and who keeps his garments, lest he walk naked and they see his shame. The first man knew himself to have been stripped of these garments when he said: “I heard, Lord, your voice, and I hid myself, because I was naked” (Gen. 3:9). Had he kept them well, neither his shame nor ours would have appeared.

It follows: “And he shall gather them into the place called in Hebrew Armageddon.”  
[Note: Codex Vaticanus: “Mageddon.”]  
Mageddon is the place in which, as is read in the books of Kings and Chronicles, the most righteous King Josiah was slain (2 Chron. 35:22). Of this place the prophet Zechariah also speaks in the person of the Lord coming to judgement, saying: “And they shall look upon me whom they crucified” (Zech. 12:10). And a little later: “On that day there shall be a great mourning in Jerusalem, like the mourning at Remmon in the plain of Mageddon; and the families of the land shall mourn, each family separately” (ibid. 12:11–12). They shall therefore be gathered in the plain called in Hebrew Armageddon—that is, before the face of God Almighty, who shall look upon them not as one about to test them, but as one about to judge them.
